\item a negative answer to (R1) together with a positive answer to (R2) (for instance through (R3)), i.e.\ N17.B$'$ in two nested worlds, applies verbatim on each $R_{ij}$: every world of a cover of $T_1$ with nested edges would have a strictly positive charge endorsing its edge comparisons on each $R_{ij}$. For leading charges (now without (Nest$_e$), Theorem~\ref{thm:S21}) and Savage measures, positivity globalises through the linking sets $R_{ij}\cap R_{ik}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:Q36}); for a general acceptance cone it does not, and one further step is needed: that no $\neg$SP$^{\mathrm{reg}}$ certificate is carried only by comparisons out of interior selected models with crossing error sets (\src{Q1} Q1.C5; by \src{N17} N17.3 such a certificate, if of type (M1), uses at least four cyclic comparisons with overlapping gains). Round 14: positivity also globalises from leading densities on the two edge regions (Theorem~\ref{thm:B13}), but not from the edge comparisons alone (Proposition~\ref{prop:B1cex}). Round 15: for a world that is $\Gamma$-leading for finitely generated $\Gamma_{ij},\Gamma_{ik}$ with (UI), the further step is exactly Question~C1.Q of part~(f) (Theorem~\ref{thm:C17}, Proposition~\ref{prop:C19}). Round 16: (R2) has a negative answer and N17.B$'$ fails in two nested worlds (Theorem~\ref{thm:D21}), so this route cannot be completed as stated; its analogue with densities locally integrable on $U$ (Conjecture~\ref{conj:sigmaB}) is false too (Theorem~\ref{thm:F13}), its analogue on $M$ (Conjecture~\ref{conj:F1Cp}) is open, and the mechanism of Theorem~\ref{thm:D21} cannot carry a cover of $T_1$ in which every world is an end-protected decoration with integrable, jointly end-heavy base densities (Theorem~\ref{thm:E15}; audited in \src{F2}, audit refereed once); round 17 removes the heaviness and excludes more (Theorems~\ref{thm:H12}, \ref{thm:H13}, Proposition~\ref{prop:HR1}; part~(f$'$));
\item independently, the first case of Theorem~\ref{thm:R3} should be excluded: that at some world the comparisons out of $T_1$ admit no strictly positive endorsing shadow. This is a statement about $T_1$'s out-comparisons at one world only; Lemma~IC (\src{R11}) and the bathtub structure of $\mathcal N_i$ are the natural tools. Excluding it puts every cover in case (ii), so unendorsed relevant comparisons against incoherent $X_k\to T_1$ are always present, and Proposition~\ref{prop:Q38} then makes far dominators cost a far tie partner or a failure of (LC$_{T_1}$). Round 16: Theorem~\ref{thm:E12} (proved in a note, audited in \src{F2}, audit refereed once) gives unendorsed comparisons against incoherent models within $\eta$ of $T_1$ without excluding case~(i), with admissible shadows in place of shadows in $\mathcal N$ (the dominator may then be $T_1$ itself), and by Theorem~\ref{thm:E11} the argument of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed} never uses $T_1$'s out-comparisons; so excluding case~(i) is no longer needed for that purpose.
\end{itemize}
\emph{Three worlds: questions from rounds 14 to 22.}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Finitely additive gluing.} Are leading charges of world $i$ on $R_{ij}$ and on $R_{ik}$ that are positive on $Q_i$ proportional there? A positive answer would extend Corollary~\ref{cor:B14} to finitely additive edge charges (scope remark in its status).
\item \emph{Total worlds.} Conjecture~\ref{conj:B3C}: every total world of a ranking with strict (G), (IB) and (S) on $\M_U$ is AR. Its first test is the order-theoretic Conjecture~\ref{conj:B3Cp}. If it holds, every world of a cover of $T_1$ that does not add up is not total.
\item \emph{Credal edges.} Question~C1.Q of part~(f): can a non-total world that is $\Gamma$-leading for finitely generated $\Gamma_{ij},\Gamma_{ik}$ with (UI) carry a finite $\Gamma^{\mathrm{gl}}$-obstruction? A negative answer excludes every such world from covers of $T_1$.
\item \emph{Density-unanimity edges.} Conjecture~\ref{conj:C2C}: in three worlds with every axiom, a world that is a density unanimity on both of its edge regions has proportional members, hence a leading density on both, hence adds up. A counterexample needs aligned pricing of the link class and interior selected models that are Bayes for every member at once.
\item \emph{Other edge orders.} Worlds without a leading density on some edge region whose edge orders are neither density unanimities nor $\Gamma$-leading for finitely generated pairs with (UI) (for instance non-Archimedean edge orders, or $\Gamma$-leading only for pairs without (UI)) are not covered by any result above. By Corollary~\ref{cor:C25}, an exclusion of such worlds, like any proof of (LD) for $n=3$, must use an input beyond the restriction of the ranking to one edge: the third world, the link class, interior indices, or the shape of coherent edge models in $\R^3$.
\item \emph{At $T_1$ itself.} Case (i) of Theorem~\ref{thm:R3} (the third item of the lifting list above); after Theorem~\ref{thm:E12} its exclusion is no longer needed to obtain unendorsed comparisons near $T_1$.
\item \emph{$\sigma$-finite endorsement} (round 16; audit of 15 October). Conjecture~\ref{conj:sigmaB} (a countably additive endorsing measure with an a.e.\ positive density, locally integrable on $U$) is false (Theorem~\ref{thm:F13}); Theorem~\ref{thm:D21} already shows that the bounded form fails. Its repair, Conjecture~\ref{conj:F1Cp} (local integrability on $M$), is open, and its use for $T_1$ depends on (Nest$_e$) (caveat in its status). The weaker a.e.-finite target of part~(e) is open, and must be read with endorsement in the cancellation form or with finite cost of the left-hand model. In two worlds next to an additive world, whether a $\sigma$-finite endorser always exists is \src{F1}'s Conjecture~F1.C. For $T_1$ the question is whether Proposition~\ref{prop:M0} survives for such measures (status of Conjecture~\ref{conj:sigmaB}), and whether Theorems~\ref{thm:E11} and~\ref{thm:E15} extend to shadows that are non-integrable only at ends. Round 17 proves this when only one world's density is non-integrable and the other two worlds have integrable full endorsers (Theorem~\ref{thm:H12}); it is open for two or more such worlds (case (D) of part~(f$'$)). Round 19 proves it for several such worlds whenever a patch exists (Theorem~\ref{thm:K35}, Corollary~\ref{cor:K35p}); what is left is sheltering and infinite minority mass.
\item \emph{Conflict cycles, and the cases outside class (EP)} (rounds 17 and 19; \src{H1}, \src{H2}, \src{H12\_referee}, \src{J1}, \src{J1\_referee}, \src{K1}, \src{K1\_referee}). Question~J1.Q: can a doubly misaligned $2$-cycle whose third world is incident to no arrow carry the shell exchanges of Proposition~\ref{prop:J15} under every axiom, for every tuple of integrable base endorsers? Question~J1.Q$'$: can a ranking in class (EP) in which no order of the worlds is aligned cover $T_1$? Question~J1.Q$'_\infty$: the same for class (EP$_\infty$) with (Al$_\infty$). \src{J1} states that a negative answer to J1.Q would exclude every cover in class (EP); that inference is unproved (\src{J1\_referee} \S8.2): a negative answer closes only case (R-i), and cases (R-ii) and (R-iii) remain. No conjecture is stated. Outside class (EP): case (A$'$), case (B) with countably many ends, case (D), and protection not of end type. \src{D2}'s Conjecture~D2.C (installing the world of Theorem~\ref{thm:D21} on an edge region) is open; next to two worlds with integrable full endorsers, an installation that keeps an a.e.\ finite endorser of its base in the cancellation form is excluded (Theorem~\ref{thm:H12}), with no condition of heaviness or compatibility.
\item \emph{Worlds without a localizable endorser, and finite certificates} (round 19; \src{K2}, \src{K3}, \src{K2\_referee}, \src{K3\_referee}). Question~Q$_{\mathrm{K3}}$: can a world of a full system have a non-null non-localizable blind set $\Lambda_\infty$? Round 20: Yes, in two worlds next to an additive world (Theorem~\ref{thm:L24}), so Conjecture~\ref{conj:K3C} is false; the open form is the one aimed at $T_1$, with a world that is not (Loc), i.e.\ in (N) (Corollary~\ref{cor:L26}; Conjecture~\ref{conj:L2C} says (N) is empty in two worlds next to an additive world). Question~Q$_{\mathrm A}$: can an integrable field with one component vanishing on a set of the rigid shape of Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}(b$'$) have property ($\gamma$) and $T_1$ as a Bayes model at an interior weight? Proposition~\ref{prop:KQA} gives necessary conditions and locates where the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) breaks. Round 20: answered No (Theorem~\ref{thm:L1}, modulo Lemma~\ref{lem:L17} and Theorem~\ref{thm:L1C}). Question~Q-K2: is there a full system with two worlds additive with integrable densities whose third world has a certificate? Conjecture~\ref{conj:K26p}: a Bayes-shaped selection over such worlds forces the third world to add up; for the Brier base, by Proposition~\ref{prop:KR62}, it reduces to the passage from the closed convex hull of the forced cone to the acceptance set.
\item \emph{The configurations of the reduction theorem} (rounds 20--22; \S\ref{sec:fixedpoint}(j)). Question~Q$_{\mathrm S}$ (\cfg{S}); Questions~Q$^{(3)}_{\mathrm{N2}}$ and Q$_{\mathrm{N2}}$ (\cfg{V0}); Question~Q$_{\mathrm{V+}}$, the $T_1$-aimed form of Question~Q$_{\mathrm{L2}}$ (\cfg{V+}); Conjecture~\ref{conj:L1D} in its rigid form (\cfg{P0}); Question~Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$ restricted to \cfg{PD}, \cfg{E} and \cfg{X}. Also open: Conjecture~\ref{conj:N1C} (the restricted crossing conjecture; \src{N1}'s N1.C as stated is false), Conjecture~\ref{conj:L2C}, the precise-edge residual of Proposition~\ref{prop:L36}(b), Theorem~\ref{thm:L35} without (N$_\infty$), and the worlds failing (NC) next to a partner that is not (RL) (Proposition~\ref{prop:M27}).
\end{itemize}
\emph{Off the $U$-domain.}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item Additive rankings with integral penalties are excluded on every decomposable domain with (LF) (Theorem~\ref{thm:gm}); with bounded charge penalties, given interior Bayes minimisers (Corollary~\ref{cor:gmcharges}).
\item Rankings whose worlds all add up: Claim~B2.0 (the transfer of Proposition~\ref{prop:M0}) is now proved (Corollary~\ref{cor:M35}, round 20, refereed once), so apex ties at the target weighting are excluded on every decomposable domain (Corollary~\ref{cor:B22}), and Corollary~\ref{cor:D17} holds at the status of Theorem~\ref{thm:D1}. On every domain with (LF) and (Av), in particular on every domain two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$, rankings whose worlds all add up are excluded (Corollary~\ref{cor:M310p}; CHECKED at Proposition~\ref{prop:M39}, pending its fixable gap (ii)). \subsection{The fixed-point reduction}\label{sec:fixedpoint}
\emph{Rounds 20 to 22.} Round 20 (\src{BRIEF17}) asked once more to settle $T_1$: either by a genuine impossibility result, or by a bolder construction of the world rankings. The brief observed that every exclusion so far exhibits one admissible shadow and shows that it is not defeated, so that a cover must defeat \emph{every} admissible shadow, including shadows adapted to the ranking. Eleven notes were written: \src{L1}--\src{L4}, \src{M1}--\src{M3}, and the round-20 parts of \src{N1} and \src{N2}. None produced a cover, and none settles $T_1$. What they give is a reduction. In every ranking with (H$_U$) in which each world satisfies a finiteness condition, (NC), every tuple of Hahn--Banach endorsers is an undefeated shadow. Its countably additive field has a coherent Bayes model at every weight and has $T_1$ as a Bayes model at some weight. If that field is strictly signed, Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) gives a contradiction. So a cover needs a \emph{degenerate} fixed point, one whose densities vanish on non-null \emph{blind sets}, and the notes determine which degeneracies survive. In round~21 an integrator's note, \src{R21}, assembled the results into one reduction theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:R21}, part~(j)). Round~22 refereed the last two notes. The referee reports are \src{L1\_referee} (on \src{L1}), \src{L23\_referee} (on \src{L2} and \src{L3}), \src{L4\_referee} (on \src{L4}), \src{M1\_referee} (on \src{M1}), \src{M23\_referee} (on \src{M2} and \src{M3}) and \src{N12\_referee} (on the top part of \src{N1} and on Part~I of \src{N2}). No referee found an error in a main line. One conjecture (N1.C) is false as stated, one stated equivalence (in \src{N2} Corollary~N2.6(a)) is wrong, and there are gaps and overstatements of wording; all are recorded below, and the referees' versions are used. Unless stated otherwise, every result of this subsection is \emph{proved in a note and confirmed by one referee}. Results first proved in a referee report are marked so (one reader), and so are the elementary inferences first made in \src{R21}, which no referee has read. In this subsection \src{N1} and \src{N2} mean the round-20 parts at the top of those files; elsewhere in the write-up they mean the earlier notes kept at the end of the same files. The round-22 results of \src{P1} are under review and are not used here, except for one sentence at Question~Q$_{\mathrm{N2}}$ in part~(j). No assumption is added anywhere.

\paragraph{Notation.} Throughout, $n=3$, $U=D_{K'}$ with $K'=u+s(T_1-u)$, and $M$, $N_+$, $\sigma_k$, $P_k$, $E_k$, $Q_l$ and $R_{ij}$ are as in \S\ref{sec:open-core}; so is (H$_U$). For $\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}$:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item $J_l\coloneqq Q_l\cap E_i(T_1)=Q_l\cap E_j(T_1)$ is the \emph{joint $T_1$-error set} of worlds $i$ and $j$ (on $Q_l$ these two worlds agree, and $T_1$ errs at both); $W_l$ is the set of $g\in M$ at which $T_1$ is wrong at world $l$ only. On $R_{ij}$, $E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}=W_i\cup J_j$, and we write $c^{ij}_T\coloneqq E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$.
\item $Y_l$ is the model equal to $T_1$ on $R_{ij}$ and to $P_i$ ($=P_j$) on $Q_l$, accepting $N_+$; it is $T_1$ with its joint errors on $J_l$ removed.
\item $\mathfrak W_k$ is the set of vectors of the relevant world-$k$ comparisons and $\mathfrak N_k\coloneqq\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W_k)$ the set of bounded endorsers of world $k$ (part~(f$''$) of \S\ref{sec:open-core}). \textbf{(NC)} at world $k$ is (NC$_{\mathfrak W_k}$): no finite nonnegative combination of members of $\mathfrak W_k$ is $\le-1$ a.e.\ on $M$. A world that fails (NC) is \emph{strongly (M1)}. (NC) holds at every world not in mode (M1), and it may hold at an (M1) world, since a certificate need not be $\le-1$.
\item By Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(a), $\mathfrak N_k\ne\varnothing$ iff (NC) holds at $k$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(c) there is then a \emph{maximal} endorser $\nu^*_k\in\mathfrak N_k$ whose density $\rho^*_k$ is positive exactly off the \emph{blind set} $\Lambda_k$ of world $k$ (the set $\Lambda_\varnothing$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(c), unique mod null); world $k$ adds up iff $\Lambda_k$ is null. $V_k\coloneqq M\setminus\Lambda_k$ is the \emph{visible set}.
\item A \emph{generalised shadow} is $\nu=(\nu_1,\nu_2,\nu_3)$ with $\nu_k\ge0$ in $\mathrm{ba}$. Write $\nu_k=\rho_k\mu+\pi_k$ (Yosida--Hewitt), and call $c^\nu\coloneqq(\rho_k\sigma_k)_k$, with $\rho_k\coloneqq1$ on $N_+$, its \emph{countably additive field}. An \emph{endorser tuple} has $\nu_k\in\mathfrak N_k$ for each $k$; the \emph{maximal field} is $c^*\coloneqq c^{\nu^*}$.
\item Costs: $t\cdot\nu(X)\coloneqq\sum_kt_k\nu_k(E_kX\cap M)$, and
\[\mathrm{Gap}_t(\nu)\coloneqq\inf_{C\text{ coherent}}t\cdot\nu(C)-\inf_{X\text{ regular}}t\cdot\nu(X)\ge0.\]
For a field $c=(\rho_k\sigma_k)$, $\psi^t(X)\coloneqq\sum_kt_k\int_{E_kX\cap M}\rho_k\,d\mu$ and $d_t(c)\coloneqq\inf_{C\text{ coherent}}\psi^t(C)-\min\psi^t$; the minimum is attained by every $c$-$t$-Bayes model.
\item A field has property \textbf{($\gamma_0$)} if $d_t(c)=0$ for every $t\in\Delta$. Then some $c$-$t$-Bayes model is coherent at every $t\in\Delta$, and ($\gamma_0$) implies ($\gamma$). $B_q$ and $Z_q$ are the strict Bayes set and the tie set of $c$ at $q$ (\S\ref{sec:M0}).
\item The \emph{admissible set} of $c$ is $A(c)\coloneqq\{p\in\Delta:\chi_T(g)\,p\cdot c(g)\ge0\text{ for a.e.\ }g\in M\}$, where $\chi_T\coloneqq+1$ on $D_{T_1}$ and $-1$ off it. $T_1$ is \emph{$c$-$p$-Bayes}, i.e.\ $D_{T_1}=B_p\cup S$ for a measurable $S\subseteq Z_p$, iff $p\in A(c)$; $A(c)$ is closed and convex.
\item An \emph{edge model} for $\{i,j\}$, with third world $l$, is a model equal to $P_i$ on $Q_l$ and accepting $N_+$; it is determined by its world-$i$ error set $c\subseteq R_{ij}$, and its world-$j$ error set is $R_{ij}\setminus c$. Every selected $C_q$ with $q\in[e_i,e_j]$ is an edge model (competitiveness on $\supp q$, strict (G), Lemma~\ref{lem:Q34}). For densities $\rho_i,\rho_j$ put $e_\theta\coloneqq\theta\rho_i-(1-\theta)\rho_j$ on $R_{ij}$, $\theta\in[0,1]$. An edge model is \emph{$\theta$-Bayes} if $c\subseteq\{e_\theta\le0\}$ and $R_{ij}\setminus c\subseteq\{e_\theta\ge0\}$ a.e. Its extreme versions $E^{\theta,-}$ and $E^{\theta,+}$ have world-$i$ error sets $\{e_\theta<0\}$ and $\{e_\theta\le0\}$. For $\theta\ne\theta'$, $e_\theta=e_{\theta'}$ only on the \emph{joint blind set} $\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$.
\end{itemize}
Facets, corner rays and crossings are as in \S\ref{sec:main}; the crossing of coordinate~$1$ on $F_2$ is $w_{12}=(0,-1,\kappa)$, and on $F_3$ it is $w_{13}=(0,\kappa,-1)$. Names of hypotheses and configurations in the notes that clash with names in the write-up are changed: \src{L4}'s (B1) is (OB) below; \src{L3}'s hypothesis (V) is (Pay); \src{M1}'s (W1)--(W4) are (Sh1)--(Sh4); \src{N1}'s alternatives (R), (D) are (rig), (dbl); and the configurations of \src{R21} are written in sans-serif type, \cfg{S}, \cfg{V0}, \cfg{E} and so on, because (S) and (E) name axioms.

\paragraph{(a) The Hahn--Banach fixed point (\src{L4}, \src{L4\_referee}).}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L40}
For every generalised shadow $\nu$ and every $t\in\Delta$, $\mathrm{Gap}_t(\nu)\ge d_t(c^\nu)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The sum $\pi\coloneqq\sum_k\pi_k$ is purely finitely additive, so (Step~1 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(b)) there are decreasing measurable $\Theta_m\subseteq M$ with $\mu(\Theta_m)\to0$ and $\pi(M\setminus\Theta_m)\le2^{-m}$. Let $\pi^t_\pm$ be the parts of the cost charges coming from the $\pi_k$ on $\{\sigma_k\gtrless0\}$, and $\mathrm{OPT}\coloneqq(\pi^t_-\wedge\pi^t_+)(M)$, the infimum of the purely finitely additive cost over all measurable choices of advice (the lattice formula). Take a pointwise $\psi^t$-minimiser $B$, and replace it on $\Theta_m$ by a set $A_m$ whose purely finitely additive cost is within $2^{-m}$ of $\mathrm{OPT}$. The resulting regular model has total cost at most $\min\psi^t+\mathrm{OPT}+o(1)$, by absolute continuity of the $\rho_k\mu$. Every coherent model has countably additive cost at least $\min\psi^t+d_t(c^\nu)$ and purely finitely additive cost at least $\mathrm{OPT}$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Lemma~L4.0); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S1.2), every step re-derived, one reader.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L41}
Assume (H$_U$) and (NC) at every world, and let $\nu$ be an endorser tuple.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item For every regular $X$ some $C\in\C_L$ has $C\preceq_kX$ and $\nu_k(E_kC)\le\nu_k(E_kX)$ at every world $k$. Hence $\mathrm{Gap}_t(\nu)=0$ for every $t\in\Delta$.
\item $c^\nu$ has property ($\gamma_0$): at every $t\in\Delta$ some coherent model is $c^\nu$-$t$-Bayes. If moreover $c^\nu\ne0$ a.e.\ on $M$, the strict Bayes set $B_q$ is coherent for every $q\in\Di$.
\item $D_{T_1}=B_{p^*}\cup S$ with $S\subseteq Z_{p^*}$ for some $p^*\in\Delta$.
\item If $c^\nu$ is strictly signed on $M$, then $p^*\in\Di$, and (H$_U$) is contradictory.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) Theorem~\ref{thm:kkm} gives $C\in\C_L$ with $C\preceq_kX$ at every $k$, and these comparisons are relevant, so the endorsers endorse them. (b) Lemma~\ref{lem:L40} gives $d_t\le\mathrm{Gap}_t=0$; the coherent infimum of $\psi^t$ is attained, because coherent models are compact in measure (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:H10}(a)) and $\psi^t$ is continuous in measure. For every $B_q$: on $M$, $c(g)$ is never a nonzero multiple of $\one$, so for a.e.\ direction $\delta\in\one^\perp$ the set $Z_q\cap\{\delta\cdot c=0\}$ is null; the models $B_{q+s\delta}$ are coherent for a.e.\ small $s>0$; their limits in measure are coherent (\src{H12\_referee} \S1.1); and the intersection of the limits for $\delta$ and $-\delta$ is $B_q$. This is the argument of Theorem~\ref{thm:Estructure}(d), which needs $c\ne0$ a.e. (c) Let $\Theta$ be the union of the localizing families of the $\pi_k$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(b)). For a relevant $T_1\preceq_kY$ with $Y=T_1$ on $\Theta_m$, $|\pi_k(\delta)|\le2^{-m'}$ for every $m'\ge m$, so $\int\rho_k\delta\,d\mu\ge0$. Steps 1--3 and 5 of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:H11} use no positivity and give $p^*$. (d) Step~4 of that proof uses positivity of the $\rho_k$ on $(-,-,+)\cap D_{T_1}$, $(-,+,-)\cap D_{T_1}$ and $(+,-,-)\cap D_{T_1}$, and gives $p^*\in\Di$; Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a), which does not use integrability, then applies to $c^\nu$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Thm.~L4.1); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S1.3), one reader. \emph{Repair.} The note stated the second sentence of (b) with no hypothesis. It is proved only when $c\ne0$ a.e.\ on $M$, and without that hypothesis it is false for fields with ($\gamma_0$) (\src{L4\_referee} \S1.3): set the realising field $c(g)=g$ to $0$ on a thin open cone $W$ around a ray inside $(+,-,-)\cap\{u\cdot g>0\}\cap U$; ($\gamma_0$) survives, since at each $t$ the old coherent $B_t$ is still a Bayes model, but the new $B_u=(U\cap\{u\cdot g>0\})\setminus W$ is not convex (NUMERICS, \src{l4ref\_py/ref\_checks.py} (C)). Whether a field of this kind can come from a ranking is not decided. Every later use has $c\ne0$ a.e. \emph{Reading.} For an endorser tuple, undefeatedness at every regular test is immediate from Theorem~\ref{thm:kkm}; the content is Lemma~\ref{lem:L40}. The brief's ``adaptive reweighting towards the worlds' own endorsers'' has its fixed point at the start: reweight every $\nu_k$ all the way into $\mathfrak N_k$. No Kakutani or Ky Fan argument is needed, and the closed-graph problem of part~(f$''$) (closedness in the index but not continuity in the tested model) does not arise. \emph{Withdrawn overstatements} (\src{L4\_referee} \S1.4). Only the one-way statement is proved: if the countably additive field of an endorser tuple is strictly signed, (H$_U$) is contradictory. The note's ``the theorem fails exactly when the fixed point is degenerate'' and ``the universal theorem holds iff no such weak realisation can be degenerate'' are not proved. A degenerate field need not come from a cover, and an admissible shadow that is not an endorser tuple might still be undefeated at the tests of Theorem~\ref{thm:E11}. The note's ``undefeated and gap-positive shadows exist iff (H$_U$) fails'' is wrong as written: under (H$_U$) such shadows never exist.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:L42}
On $\M_U$ no ranking with (H$_U$) has every world adding up (Definition~\ref{def:addup}, finitely additive weights allowed). This is Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(b), by a second route.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A world that adds up has a weight, positive on non-null sets, that endorses its relevant comparisons. Restricted to $M$ and normalised, it lies in $\mathfrak N_k$, and its density is positive a.e.\ on $M$ (last item of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(c), which is \src{N19} Lemma~R1). So (NC) holds at every world and $c^\nu$ is strictly signed; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(d).
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Cor.~L4.2); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S2), one reader. The referee checked that Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) applies to $c^\nu$: ($\gamma$) follows from ($\gamma_0$) and Tonelli; $c\equiv(1,1,1)$ on $N_+$ has no ties; integrability is not used. The route bypasses \src{N13} Prop.~B, \src{N19} Prop.~R3(a), \src{N17} Prop.~2.1 and (E$_\psi$). Its inputs are Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(a)--(c), Lemmas~\ref{lem:H10}(a) and~\ref{lem:H11}, each read once by a referee, \src{H12\_referee} \S1.1, Theorem~\ref{thm:kkm}, and Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a), read by two. So Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(b) now holds at the status of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31} and Lemma~\ref{lem:H11} (each read once), in place of the once-read imports named in its status. The note's remark that the same route gives Corollary~\ref{cor:CPaU}(b) is right, but it also needs Theorem~\ref{thm:fullsupport} (refereed once) for the weight of Corollary~\ref{cor:CPaU}(b) (\src{L4\_referee} \S2).}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L43}
In Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}, let $l$ be the third world. If $p^*$ lies in the open edge $(e_i,e_j)$, then $\rho_i=\rho_j=0$ a.e.\ on $J_l$. If $p^*=e_i$, then $\rho_i=0$ a.e.\ on $E_i(T_1)\cap M$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(c) gives $p^*\cdot v\ge0$ a.e.\ on $M$, with $v_k=\rho_k$ where $T_1$ is correct at $k$ and $v_k=-\rho_k$ where it is wrong. On $J_l$, $v_i=-\rho_i$ and $v_j=-\rho_j$; at $p^*=e_i$ the condition reads $v_i\ge0$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Prop.~L4.3); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S3), one reader. The sets $J_l$ are non-null: $J_3\supseteq D_{T_1}\cap(-,-,+)$ near $r_{12}$, a non-empty open set; this is a proof, and the numerics of the note are not needed.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L44}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item Let $\sum_j\lambda_j\delta_j\le0$ be a certificate at a world $k$ that satisfies (NC), and $W\coloneqq\{\sum_j\lambda_j\delta_j<0\}$. Then $\nu_k(W)=0$ for every $\nu_k\in\mathfrak N_k$. So $W\subseteq\Lambda_k$, and the purely finitely additive parts vanish on $W$ too.
\item $\Lambda_k\supseteq\Lambda_\infty$ at every world $k$ with (NC).
\item A strongly (M1) world has $\mathfrak N_k=\varnothing$; such worlds are the only worlds outside Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Prop.~L4.4(a), (b), (d)); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S3), one reader. In (a), $f=\sum_j\lambda_j\delta_j$ is simple, so $f\le-\eta$ on $W$ for some $\eta>0$, and $0\le\nu_k(f)\le-\eta\nu_k(W)$. \emph{Reading} (the note's item (c), which the referee asked to be labelled). Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} uses no patch model and no localized endorser, so the sheltering residual of Corollary~\ref{cor:K35p}(c) and case (B) of part~(f$'$) are not obstructions to it. The note's further sentences, that two worlds sheltering one another reappear only as two blind sets that meet on a common region, and that joint blindness on a joint $T_1$-error set is exactly what boundary admissibility requires, are interpretations; Proposition~\ref{prop:L43} gives a necessary condition only. \emph{Consequence.} For systems with (NC) at every world, a cover needs the maximal field $c^*$, whose blind sets are exactly the $\Lambda_k$, to have ($\gamma_0$) and to admit $T_1$, with some $\Lambda_k$ non-null (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(d) and Proposition~\ref{prop:L43}).}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L45}
There are generalised shadows $\nu$ with every $\nu_k(M)=1$, $\mathrm{Gap}_t(\nu)=0$ for every $t$, and $T_1$ $t\cdot\nu$-optimal at an interior weight.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $\pi$ be a $\{0,1\}$-valued charge, vanishing on null sets, that lives on every open cone around a ray $r\in D_{T_1}\cap(+,-,-)$ (an ultrafilter containing these cones and the co-null sets), and put $\nu_1=\nu_2=\nu_3=\pi$. A model costs $t_2+t_3$ if it accepts near $r$ and $t_1$ otherwise; $T_1$ and $P_2$ are coherent and realise both values. $T_1$ is optimal at $t=(3/4,1/8,1/8)$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Prop.~L4.5); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S3), one reader. So no argument that uses only the zero gap of the fixed point can reach a contradiction; positivity of the countably additive part is the whole content. Whether such a purely finitely additive $\nu$ can be the endorser tuple of a ranking with (H$_U$) is not decided.}

\paragraph{(b) One blind world (\src{L4}, \src{L4\_referee}).} \textbf{Hypothesis (OB).} $c=(\rho_1\sigma_1,\rho_2\sigma_2,\rho_3\sigma_3)$ is measurable, with $\rho_2,\rho_3>0$ a.e.\ on $M$ and $\rho_1\ge0$; $\Lambda_1\coloneqq\{\rho_1=0\}\cap M$; $c$ has ($\gamma_0$) (or merely ($\gamma$)); and $D_{T_1}=B_{p^*}\cup S$ with $S\subseteq Z_{p^*}$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} this is the situation of every cover in which worlds~2 and~3 add up and world~1 satisfies (NC): take $\nu=(\nu^*_1,\text{weight}_2,\text{weight}_3)$. Then $p^*\in\Di$ unless $p^*=e_1$ and $\Lambda_1\supseteq E_1(T_1)\cap M$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:L43} and step~4 of Lemma~\ref{lem:H11}). The proofs of Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}(b), (b$'$) and of Proposition~\ref{prop:KQA}(a) use only ($\gamma$), $\rho_2,\rho_3>0$ and $\rho_1>0$ off $\Lambda_1$ (re-read in \src{L4\_referee} \S4.1), so they hold under (OB) with $\Lambda_1$ in place of $\Lambda_\infty$. We use their notation: the splices $S_\theta$, and the credal sets $K_1$ of $S_1$ and $K_0$ of $S_0$, with $K_1\cap[e_1,e_2]\ne\varnothing$, $K_1\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_2])$, $K_0\cap[e_1,e_3]\ne\varnothing$, $K_0\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_3])$, $\Lambda_1\cap R_{12}=E_1(D_{K_1})\cap R_{12}$ and $\Lambda_1\cap R_{13}=E_1(D_{K_0})\cap R_{13}$. Let $L^*$ be the line through $e_1$ and $p^*$, and $\theta^*\coloneqq p^*_2/(p^*_2+p^*_3)$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L46}
Assume (OB) with $p^*\in\Di$.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item \emph{Vertex fan.} As $q\to e_1$ in $\Di$, every Hausdorff cluster value $\hat K$ of $K^\flat_q$ has $D_{\hat K}=P_1$ a.e.\ on $M\setminus\Lambda_1$, and $D_{\hat K}=D_{K_1}$ on $(+,-,-)$ and on $(-,+,+)$.
\item \emph{Contact.} On the open $(+,-,-)$-portions of $F_2$ and $F_3$ (corner ray $r_{23}$ and crossings excluded), $P_{K_1}>0$, equivalently $P_{K_0}>0$. Hence Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_1$ holds at every point of these portions.
\item \emph{Forced reach.} $P_{K_1}(w_{12})\le0$, with equality only if $K_1\cap[e_1,e_2]=\{e_1\}$; if $P_{K_1}(w_{12})<0$, then $\Lambda_1\supseteq(+,-,+)\cap O$ for a neighbourhood $O$ of $w_{12}$, so $\Lambda_1$ contains a two-sided conic neighbourhood of every short arc of the middle arc of $F_2$ near $w_{12}$. The same holds at $w_{13}\in F_3$ with $K_0$ and $(+,+,-)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Lemma~L4.6); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S4.1), one reader, including the step in (b) at which two distinct supporting planes through a facet point would put a point of $D_{T_1}\cap(+,-,-)$ outside $D_{K_1}$. In (b) the margin is $(1-s)\cdot2\varepsilon/3>0$: $v_3\in K_1$ or $v_2\in K_0$ would contradict $K_1\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_2])$, $K_0\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_3])$ (NUMERICS confirm the margins). In (c), $m\cdot w_{12}=-(1-a)$ for $m=(a,1-a,0)$. So unless $K_1\cap[e_1,e_2]=\{e_1\}=K_0\cap[e_1,e_3]$, the blind set reaches a coordinate-1 crossing, where the chart lines of its gambles pass through $e_1$.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L47}
Under (OB), without assuming $p^*\in\Di$, $\Lambda_1=E_1(T_1)\cap M$ (mod null) is impossible.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$S_1$ equals $T_1$ on $R_{12}$: off $\Lambda_1$, $T_1$ is world-1-correct, so $S_1=P_1=T_1$; on $\Lambda_1\cap R_{12}$, $T_1$ is world-2-correct, so $S_1=P_2=T_1$. The $r_{23}$-corner portion of $F_3$ lies, with both sides, in $Q_1\subseteq R_{12}$; the argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:L46}(b) gives $v_3\in K_1$, against the margin.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Example~L4.7); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S4.1), one reader; $p^*$ is not used. NUMERICS: the splice ``$T_1$ on $Q_1\cup Q_2$, $P_1$ on $Q_3$'' fails midpoint convexity.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L48}
Assume (OB) with $p^*\in\Di$. There is no open arc $\Gamma$ in the relative interior of a facet $F_k$, off its crossings, with an open cone $N\supseteq\Gamma$ inside one open orthant and meeting no other facet, such that $N\setminus\Lambda_1$ is null and $S\cap N$ is null.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Lemma~L4.8, with ``$Z_{p^*}\cap N$ null'' in place of ``$S\cap N$ null''); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S4.1), one reader, who strengthens the hypothesis to the form stated: steps 0--1 of the proof need only $B_{p^*}\cap N=D_{T_1}\cap N$, i.e.\ $S\cap N$ null, since ties outside $D_{T_1}$ are rejected by both. \emph{Proof idea.} In $(+,-,-)$ and $(-,+,+)$, $c=(0,-,-)$ or $(0,+,+)$ on $\Lambda_1$, so $B_{p^*}$ is constant on $N$, which $T_1$ is not; elsewhere, along $L^*\cap\Di$, $q\cdot c=(q_2+q_3)\,m(g)$ on $\Lambda_1$ with $m\coloneqq\theta^*\rho_2\sigma_2+(1-\theta^*)\rho_3\sigma_3$, so $B_q\cap N=D_{T_1}\cap N$ is frozen, $P^\flat(q,\cdot)\le0$ on $F_k$ for every $q\in L^*\cap\Di$ by concavity, and the two ends of $L^*$ (one used only for $k=1$) give coherent limits that are positive somewhere on $F_k$. The referee added the case $P^\flat<0$ of step~2.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L49}
Assume (OB) with $p^*\in\Di$. Then one of the following holds.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[(I$_2$)] $P_{K_1}(w_{12})<0$, and for every short arc $\Gamma$ of the middle arc of $F_2$ near $w_{12}$ inside $\{P_{K_1}<0\}$, and every open cone $N\supseteq\Gamma$, the set $S\cap N$ is non-null.
\item[(I$_3$)] The same at $w_{13}\in F_3$ with $K_0$.
\item[(II)] $P_{K_1}(w_{12})=0=P_{K_0}(w_{13})$.
\end{itemize}
In (I$_2$) and (I$_3$) the tie set $Z_{p^*}\cap\Lambda_1$ is non-null; it is the union of the two oriented atoms on which $c\propto\pm(0,1-\theta^*,-\theta^*)$, and their chord is $L^*$, through $e_1$.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{L4} Thm.~L4.9); confirmed (\src{L4\_referee} \S4.2), one reader. \emph{Repair.} The note's statement ``$S$ charges these atoms'' did not follow from its form of (I$_2$), since the ties might all lie outside $D_{T_1}$; with the strengthened Lemma~\ref{lem:L48} it does, and (I$_2$), (I$_3$) are stated here in that form. The description of $Z_{p^*}\cap\Lambda_1$ needs no ball lemma: on $\Lambda_1$, $p^*\cdot c=0$ iff $\rho_3/\rho_2=\theta^*/(1-\theta^*)$ with $\sigma_2\ne\sigma_3$. Configuration (I) (that is, (I$_2$) or (I$_3$)) is excluded by the next proposition, and case (II) after it.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L4R}
Under (OB) with $p^*\in\Di$, (I$_2$) and (I$_3$) are impossible.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By the transposition of worlds 2 and 3 it suffices to exclude (I$_2$). By Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(b), $B_{p^*}=D_{K^\flat}$ is coherent with $K^\flat\supseteq T_1$, and $S=D_{T_1}\setminus D_{K^\flat}$ mod null. On $F_2$, $\gamma(\tau)\coloneqq P^\flat(p^*,h(\tau))$ is concave and $\le0$; its negative set consists of an interval at $r_{12}$ and an interval at $r_{23}$, possibly empty. A flat zero of $\gamma$ on an open sub-arc near $w_{12}$ would make $D_{K^\flat}\supseteq D_{T_1}$ near it, so $S$ would be null on a small cone there, against (I$_2$); hence $\gamma<0$ on an open sub-arc $\Gamma^0$ of the middle arc near $w_{12}$, inside one of the two intervals. The shell $\{\lambda h+s\one:\lambda>0,\ h\in\alpha,\ 0<s<\lambda|\gamma(h)|\}$ over an arc $\alpha$ with $\gamma<0$ is open, connected and contained in $S\subseteq Z_{p^*}$; by the sign-free part of Lemma~\ref{lem:ball}, $c\propto b$ on it for one vector $b$. Since $0<s<|\gamma|\le-\min_ih_i$, the shell over $\Gamma^0$ meets $(+,-,+)\cap\{P_{K_1}<0\}\subseteq\Lambda_1$, so $b_1=0$ and the whole shell lies in $\Lambda_1$. If $\Gamma^0$ lies in the interval at $r_{23}$, the shell has a non-null part in $\Lambda_1\cap(+,-,-)$, where $c=(0,-,-)$ has no ties at an interior $p^*$: a contradiction. If it lies in the interval at $r_{12}$, the shell is a carrying atom $G$ with $b=(0,b_2,b_3)$, $b_2<0<b_3$, and chord $L^*\ni p^*$; Proposition~\ref{prop:carrying}(c), (d) and the last step of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a), run on $F_1$ (with $r=r_{12}$, $j=2$ and odd world~3), give $h$ with $P_{K_\delta}(h)>0\ge P_{K_\delta}(h)$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved in a referee report (\src{L4\_referee} \S4.2, where it is ``Proposition~R''), one reader. Its inputs beyond \src{L4}'s lemmas are those that the audit of case (II) below already relies on (item (iv)), so it stands at the standard of Theorem~\ref{thm:L49}. Independently, Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(a) of part~(d) excludes (I$_2$) and (I$_3$) (\src{L1\_referee} \S8). \emph{Withdrawn.} The note handed over (I) as ``the single precise obstruction'' and proposed, as a first computation, to redo Proposition~\ref{prop:T1} with a modified crossing row at $w_{12}$. In (I), $Z_{p^*}\cap\Lambda_1$ is non-null, so $p^*\in E$ and $L^*$ is an exceptional chord; the corner/box chain at $p^*$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:chainchords}) does not start, so that computation aimed at the wrong branch (\src{L4\_referee} \S6).}

\emph{Case (II).} \emph{What it looks like} (\src{L4} \S5.3; proved; confirmed, \src{L4\_referee} \S4.3). By Lemma~\ref{lem:L46}(c), $K_1\cap[e_1,e_2]=\{e_1\}=K_0\cap[e_1,e_3]$, so $D_{K_1},D_{K_0}\subseteq P_1$ and $\Lambda_1\subseteq M\cap\{g_1>0\}$: world~1 is blind only to errors of rejection. By concavity of $\tau\mapsto P_{K_1}(h(\tau))$ (positive on the $(+,-,-)$-portion, zero at $w_{12}$), $\Lambda_1$ misses a neighbourhood of every point of the open middle arcs of $F_2$, $F_3$ and of their $(+,-,-)$-portions; it misses $F_1$ and every point with $h_1<0$. So $\Lambda_1$ touches $\partial D_{T_1}\setminus0$ only along the rays $w_{12}$, $w_{13}$ and $r_{23}$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_1$ holds at every boundary gamble $x$ with $x_1\ne0$ other than $r_{23}$. \emph{The audit} (\src{L4} \S5.4; CHECKED). The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a), with the chain of \S\ref{sec:main} that Proposition~\ref{prop:chainchords} audits, uses strict signs of $c$ at world~1 in exactly four kinds of place: (i) Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_1$, in Theorem~\ref{thm:pivot} steps 0, 1, 2 and 4, in the crossing rows $\lambda_{1k}>0$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:boxbridge}(a), in Lemma~\ref{lem:nopin} at $(\kappa,-1,0)$ and $(\kappa,0,-1)$, in Lemma PL2, and in Proposition~\ref{prop:carrying}(d); (ii) the last line of Lemma~\ref{lem:ball}, for balls centred on $\{g_1=0\}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:crosspin} at $w_{12}$, $w_{13}$, Proposition~\ref{prop:chainchords}'s PL2 for $K^\flat$, Proposition~\ref{prop:carrying}(b)), and \src{N25} Thm.~4.1(a); (iii) Lemma~\ref{lem:edgebox}; (iv) ``chords miss the vertices'' (Theorem~\ref{thm:Estructure}(b)) in Proposition~\ref{prop:carrying}(d). In case (II) each is restored: (i) and (ii) by the facts just listed, (iii) because with one blind world the box is negative on every point of the open edge used, and (iv) because blind carrying atoms at $r_{12}$ and $r_{31}$ can be run on $F_1$ and those at $r_{23}$ are never blind at an interior $p^*$. \src{L4\_referee} \S5 confirms the list by its own re-derivation, at the level of the printed proofs, with four additions: (a) two steps use signs only weakly and survive $c_1=0$ (the vertex statements of Lemma~\ref{lem:chords}(b), and the inequality $(a_-)_c\le0$ in PL2); (b) Proposition~\ref{prop:T1} applies the chain to the transposed field $c^\sigma$, which is blind at world~2, and its restoration is the image of the case-(II) facts under $\sigma$, by the equivariance $B^\sigma_q=\sigma B_{\sigma q}$; (c) the remaining inputs are sign-free, and the great circle $e_1^\perp$, which may carry non-atomic mass, corresponds to $q=e_1\notin\Di$; (d) the reading is of the write-up's printed sketches, and the source proofs behind them (\src{R10b} Lemmas UVN, D, M; \src{N15}; \src{N12}; \src{P4} Lemmas 2.4--2.5; \src{N25} Lemma~3.1 and Thm.~3.3) were not re-read for sign use. So case (II) is excluded at CHECKED level. It is also an instance of Theorem~\ref{thm:L1C} (\src{L1\_referee} \S8): two CHECKED readings of overlapping material.

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:L4V}
Assume (H$_U$), let worlds 2 and 3 add up, and let world 1 satisfy (NC). Then, for the maximal endorser tuple, $T_1$ is $c^*$-Bayes only at $p^*=e_1$, and $\Lambda_1\supsetneq E_1(T_1)\cap M$.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved in a referee report (\src{L4\_referee} \S0), from Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}, Lemma~\ref{lem:L46}, Proposition~\ref{prop:L47}, Lemma~\ref{lem:L48}, Theorem~\ref{thm:L49} and Proposition~\ref{prop:L4R}, one reader; except case (II), which is CHECKED. This is configuration \cfg{V} of Theorem~\ref{thm:R21}, the only remaining one-blind-world configuration; the referee recommends it as the main theorem of \src{L4}. It holds for every world~1 with (NC), including (M1) worlds whose certificates are not $\le-1$.}

\paragraph{(c) Partners with leading densities: the forced fixed point (\src{M2}, \src{M23\_referee}).} \textbf{(RL)} at a world $j\ne1$: there is $\rho_j\in L^1(M)$, $\rho_j>0$ a.e., such that, with $\psi_j(X)\coloneqq\int_{E_jX\cap M}\rho_j\,d\mu$, for every $C\in\C_L$ and every regular $X$: (RL-1) $\psi_j(C)<\psi_j(X)$ implies $C\preceq_jX$; (RL-2) $C\preceq_jX$ implies $\psi_j(C)\le\psi_j(X)$. (RL-2) says that $\rho_j\mu$ endorses every relevant comparison; (RL-1) adds that every $\psi_j$-strict worsening of a member of $\C_L$ is accepted. A leading density (part~(f)) satisfies both, by (L1) and \src{B1} Lemma~B1.0; so do additive worlds with integrable densities and their lexicographic refinements (\src{M23\_referee} \S1.1). (RL) implies (NC), since $\rho_j\mu/\rho_j(M)$ is then an endorser (\src{R21}, elementary). Assume (RL) at every world $j\ne1$. A \emph{forced pair} is $(C,X)$ with $C\in\C_L$, $X$ regular, and some $S\ni1$ such that $C$ is competitive on $S$ and $\psi_j(X)<\psi_j(C)$ for every $j\in S\setminus\{1\}$; examples are $C=C_q$ with $S=\supp q\ni1$, and $C=T_1$ with $S=\Omega$ ($T_1$ is competitive on $\Omega$ by \src{R11} Lemma~IC). A \emph{limit pair} is $(C_{q^*},X)$ such that some $q_m\to q^*$ with constant support $S\ni1$ have $\psi_j(X)<\liminf_m\psi_j(C_{q_m})$ for every $j\in S\setminus\{1\}$. $\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1$ is the set of world-1 vectors of forced and limit pairs; $\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1\subseteq\mathfrak W_1$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M21}
Let every world $j\ne1$ satisfy (RL) ($n\ge2$, any $K'\subseteq\Di$; strict (G), (IB), (LA), (S)).
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item $q\mapsto\psi_j(C_q)$ is lower semicontinuous on $\Delta$.
\item Every forced pair and every limit pair $(C,X)$ has $C\preceq_1X$, and its vector is divisible (part~(f$''$), \src{K2}).
\item $\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1)\ne\varnothing$, and some $\varphi^*\in\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1)$ has a density that is positive exactly off a set $\Lambda^\natural$, minimal mod null. If world~1 satisfies (NC), then $\Lambda^\natural\subseteq\Lambda_1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M2} Lemmas~M2.1, M2.2, Cor.~M2.3); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S\S1.2--1.3), one reader. (c) is Theorem~\ref{thm:K21} applied to accepted divisible vectors, then Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(a), (c) for the family $\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1$. \emph{Wording repair.} The note says these hold ``with no hypothesis on world~1 beyond strict (G) and (IB)''; competitiveness of $C_q$ and of $T_1$ at world~1 and world~1's closed sections are used too. Both are part of the standing hypotheses. The correct phrase is ``with no (NC), additivity or endorsement hypothesis on world~1''.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M24}
Let every world $j\ne1$ satisfy (RL) ($n\ge2$, any target), let $\varphi\in\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1)$ and $\nu\coloneqq(\varphi,\rho_2\mu,\dots,\rho_n\mu)$. Then $\mathrm{Gap}_t(\nu)=0$ for every $t\in\Delta$, the coherent infimum being approached by selected models; hence $c^\nu$ has ($\gamma_0$).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Fix $t$, a regular $B$ and $\eta>0$. On a small non-null $W\subseteq\{h\in M:\sigma_j(h)=-\sigma_1(h)\text{ for all }j\ne1\}$ off the carrier of the purely finitely additive part of $\varphi$, let $B_-$ and $B_+$ equal $B$ off $W$ and take on $W$ the side of the partner worlds and of world~1 respectively; then $\psi_j(B_+)-\psi_j(B_-)=\rho_j\mu(W)>0$ for every $j\ne1$. Run the KKM lemma with the closed sets $F_j\coloneqq\{q:C_q\preceq_jB_+\}$ ($j\ne1$) and $F_1\coloneqq\cl O$, where $O$ is the set of $q$ with $1\in\supp q$ and $C_q\not\preceq_jB_+$ for every $j\in\supp q\setminus\{1\}$; competitiveness gives the covering condition. At the common point $q^*$, (RL-2) bounds $\psi_j(C_{q^*})$ for $j\ne1$; along $q_m\in O$ with constant support, the contrapositive of (RL-1) gives $\liminf_m\psi_j(C_{q_m})\ge\psi_j(B_+)>\psi_j(B_-)$, so $(C_{q^*},B_-)$ is a limit pair and $\varphi$ endorses it. Lemma~\ref{lem:L40} then gives ($\gamma_0$).
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{M2} Thm.~M2.4); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S2), one reader. The strict inequality required of a limit pair is supplied by the perturbation $B_\pm$, not by the limit. The point $q^*$ may have $1\notin\supp q^*$; this is harmless, because the definition of a limit pair constrains only the approximating sequence and world~1's section is closed on all of $\Delta$. NUMERICS (an additive Brier system; world~1 is additive there, so the case of a world~1 without (NC) is not exercised).}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M25}
Assume (H$_U$), let worlds 2 and 3 satisfy (RL), let $\varphi\in\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1)$, and let $\rho_1$ be its countably additive density. Then $T_1$ is $c$-$p^*$-Bayes for $c=(\rho_k\sigma_k)$ and some $p^*\in\Delta$, and either $p^*\in\Di$, or $p^*=e_1$ and $\rho_1=0$ a.e.\ on $E_1(T_1)\cap M$.
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{M2} Prop.~M2.5); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S3), one reader. For $W$ off the carrier of the purely finitely additive part, $(T_1,T_1\sd W)$ is a forced pair whenever $T_1\sd W$ is better than $T_1$ at worlds~2 and~3, and that part vanishes \emph{exactly} on its vector; Lyapunov and separation from the open negative orthant give the weight. The referee checked all three boundary cases.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M26}
Assume (H$_U$), and let worlds 2 and 3 satisfy (RL); world~1 is arbitrary (strongly (M1) allowed). Then the field $c=(\rho_1\sigma_1,\rho_2\sigma_2,\rho_3\sigma_3)$, with $\rho_1$ the density of $\varphi^*$, satisfies (OB) with $\Lambda_1\coloneqq\Lambda^\natural$. Hence either (H$_U$) is contradictory, or $p^*=e_1$ and $\Lambda^\natural\supsetneq E_1(T_1)\cap M$.
\end{theorem}
\status{The first sentence: proved (\src{M2} Thm.~M2.6); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S4), one reader. ($\gamma_0$) is Theorem~\ref{thm:M24}; $B_q$ is coherent for every $q\in\Di$ because $c\ne0$ a.e.\ (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(b) with the referee's hypothesis); admissibility is Proposition~\ref{prop:M25}. If $\Lambda^\natural$ is null, $p^*=e_1$ is impossible and Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) applies. Its ``Q$_{\mathrm{M2}}$ \ldots second part answered no'' overclaims: what is shown is that a world failing (NC) next to two (RL) partners creates no configuration beyond those available to (NC) worlds, which after the sharpening is \cfg{V} alone; whether \cfg{V} occurs is open.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M27}
In Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}, (NC) at world $k$ can be replaced by (NC) for the family $\mathfrak D_k\cup\mathfrak T_k$, where $\mathfrak D_k$ is the set of vectors $1_{E_kX}-1_{E_kC}$ with $C$ selected, $X$ regular and $C\preceq_iX$ at every $i$ (the dominance pairs of Theorem~\ref{thm:kkm}), and $\mathfrak T_k$ the set of vectors $1_{E_kY}-1_{E_kT_1}$ of the relevant comparisons $T_1\preceq_kY$.
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{M2} Prop.~M2.7, by inspection of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S5), one reader. $\mathfrak T_k$ alone satisfies (NC), and indeed (NC$^+$) (one base; \src{N17} Lemma~3.1). \emph{The obstruction left} (\src{M2} \S6, corrected). Theorem~\ref{thm:M24} needs (RL-1) at every partner, in two places, Lemma~\ref{lem:M21}(a) and step~3 of the proof (\src{M23\_referee} \S5; the note said ``exactly one place''). Without (RL-1) at a partner $j$, the failure of competitiveness at $j$ carries no $\psi_j$-information, and the world-1 comparison handed over by competitiveness may be rigid, out of reach of Theorem~\ref{thm:K21}. So the residual is a world failing (NC) one of whose partners is not (RL), for instance a unanimity of several densities. Nothing shows that such worlds exist or that they do not. \emph{Why (NC) was not proved} (a reading, CHECKED): strict (G), (IB) and sum closure do not exclude uniformly negative certificates, nor does coherence of the bases; a proof must use (S) or (C) on rigid comparisons.}

\paragraph{(d) Weak fields (\src{L1}, \src{L1\_referee}).} This part answers Question~Q$_{\mathrm A}$ of part~(f$''$) of \S\ref{sec:open-core}. \emph{Standing data:} $c=(\rho_1\sigma_1,\rho_2\sigma_2,\rho_3\sigma_3)$ measurable on $U$, with $\rho_2,\rho_3>0$ a.e., $\rho_1>0$ a.e.\ on $M\setminus\Lambda$ and $\rho_1=0$ on a non-null $\Lambda\subseteq M$; property ($\gamma$); and $D_{T_1}=B_{p^*}\cup S$ with $S\subseteq Z_{p^*}$ for some $p^*\in\Di$. Write $\theta(q)\coloneqq q_2/(q_2+q_3)$, $\theta^*\coloneqq\theta(p^*)$, and $R^*\coloneqq L^*$ for the line through $e_1$ and $p^*$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L1}
Under the standing data there is a contradiction: no field of this kind has $D_{T_1}$ as a Bayes model at an interior weight. Integrability is not used.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{L1} Thm.~L1) \emph{modulo} Lemma~\ref{lem:L17} (a gap, repaired by Lemma~\ref{lem:L17z}) and Theorem~\ref{thm:L1C} (CHECKED); the label is right once Corollary~\ref{cor:L1B} is relabelled (\src{L1\_referee} \S0). So Question~Q$_{\mathrm A}$ has answer \emph{No}, at that status. With Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}: next to two worlds with integrable densities that endorse all their relevant comparisons, the third world of a cover is in mode (M1) or has $\Lambda_\infty\supseteq E_1(T_1)\cap M$ (\src{L1} \S6.1, confirmed), and by Proposition~\ref{prop:L47} the inclusion is strict. \emph{Why it is not routine} (Proposition~\ref{prop:L12}): blind sets can defeat the corner/box algebra, so the proof uses something other than the corner equation against the box: frozenness along rays from $e_1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:L16}).}

\emph{Bayes structure} (\src{L1} \S\S1.1--1.2; confirmed, \src{L1\_referee} \S1). On $\Lambda$, $q\cdot c=(q_2+q_3)\bigl(\theta\rho_2\sigma_2+(1-\theta)\rho_3\sigma_3\bigr)$: the advice depends on $q$ only through $\theta(q)$. So the chart lines of $\Lambda\cap R_{23}$ pass through $e_1$, the charts on $\Lambda\cap\{\sigma_2=\sigma_3\}$ are $\varnothing$ or $\Di$, the ties on $\Lambda$ have $c\propto\pm(0,1-\theta,-\theta)$ with chords $\{\theta=\mathrm{const}\}$ through $e_1$, and along $\{\theta=\theta_0\}$, $B_q\to S_{\theta_0}$ in measure: a fan of vertex limits at $e_1$. Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_1$ holds at a mixed $x$ \emph{when} some ball around $x$ meets $\Lambda$ in a null set (the note's ``exactly when'' is an overstatement: at a pinned crossing with an outside $\Lambda$-cusp it holds by concavity from the neighbours; referee). An \emph{$R^*$-arc} is an open facet arc $J$ with a conic neighbourhood inside $\Lambda$; an \emph{int-$\Lambda$ point} is a facet point with such a neighbourhood. \emph{Necessary conditions} (\src{L1} \S1.3; confirmed): the rigidity of Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}(b$'$); Proposition~\ref{prop:KQA}(a); and the exclusions from ``between'': $v_3\notin\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_2])\supseteq K_1$ and $v_2\notin\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_3])\supseteq K_0$, with margin $(1-s)\cdot2\varepsilon/3$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L12}
Suppose $\Lambda$ contains conic neighbourhoods of the two coordinate-1 crossings $w_{12}$ and $w_{13}$, so that the facet chords there are pinned to $R^*$. Then the corner equations and the crossing boxes of \S\ref{sec:main} are simultaneously satisfiable, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$.
\end{proposition}
\status{proved as algebra (\src{L1} Prop.~L1.2); confirmed (\src{L1\_referee} \S3), constraints re-derived by hand, one reader. NUMERICS: an independent exact per-pair box test at $\varepsilon=0.3$ finds no violation among 766\,042 admissible pairs (\src{l1ref\_py/twoarc\_exact.py}). The configuration is hypothetical: Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(a) excludes it. Its role is diagnostic: no contradiction can come from the corner equations and boxes alone once $\Lambda$ holds neighbourhoods of $w_{12}$ and $w_{13}$.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L13}
Let $b$ be a coordinate and $a\ne b$, and let $w_A$, $w_B$ be crossings of coordinate $b$ on rotating facet pieces with $w_{A,a}<0<w_{B,a}$, with pinned rows $c_b(h)=\lambda h_b$ near each. Then the edge box of Proposition~\ref{prop:boxbridge}(c) holds for all pairs near $(w_A,w_B)$ iff $\lambda_B\,|c_a(w_A)|\,w_{B,a}\ge\lambda_A\,c_a(w_B)\,|w_{A,a}|$. In the strict normalisation of Proposition~\ref{prop:T1} the six instances are the bounds $1/\kappa\le x_kx_{k+1}\le\kappa$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:P1box}.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{L1} Lemma~L1.3); confirmed (\src{L1\_referee} \S3), one reader, and shown sharp numerically (\src{l1ref\_py/box\_sharpness.py}: violations appear just past the predicted threshold, only at pairs near the crossings). Grid checks of the boxes miss these crossing limits; every feasibility claim uses the exact formula.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L16}
Let $N\subseteq\Lambda$ be a conic neighbourhood of a compact facet arc $J_0$. For $q,q'\in\Di$ with $\theta(q)=\theta(q')$, $B_q\cap N=B_{q'}\cap N$ and $Z_q\cap N=Z_{q'}\cap N$; so, for $h\in J_0$ and small values, $P^\flat(q,h)$ depends on $\theta(q)$ only, and on $R^*\cap\Di$ it equals $P^\flat(p^*,h)$.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{L1} Lemma~L1.6); confirmed (\src{L1\_referee} \S4), one reader. The form used later is that clipped values of $P^\flat(q,h)$ are functions of $B_q\cap N$. Lemma L1.4 of the note (every $B_q$ coherent, face models, a weak ball lemma, crosspin at the crossings of coordinates~2 and~3, local UVN at $e_1$) is confirmed, with one added line in its local-UVN part (upward closure of $D_K$).}

\emph{Auxiliary positive gambles} (\src{L1} \S4; confirmed). For each facet there are a gamble $h_0$ on its line, $t>0$ and an open $W\subseteq\Di$ meeting every ray $\{\theta=\mathrm{const}\}$ from $e_1$, with $P^\flat(q,h_0)\ge t$ on $W$: on $F_1$, a middle-arc point, forced positive by worlds 2 and 3 on a strip along $(e_2,e_3)$; on $F_2$, $F_3$, a strict point of the $(+,-,-)$-arc, forced positive by world~1 near $e_1$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L1A}
Under the standing data:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item no facet point of $D_{T_1}$ is an int-$\Lambda$ point;
\item no open facet arc is one-sidedly adjacent to $\Lambda$ (adjacent on one side, with $D_{K_*}$, $K_*\in\{K_1,K_0\}$, sharing the facet there).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof idea of (a)]
On a conic neighbourhood $N\subseteq\Lambda$ of an arc of int-$\Lambda$ points the ties at $p^*$ form one oriented atom family, and the two tie-breakings give face models $L_+\subseteq D_{T_1}\cap N\subseteq L_-$. If $P_{L_-}$ vanishes on a subarc, then, by Lemma~\ref{lem:L16}, along every ray from $e_1$ near $R^*$ the values $P^\flat(q,\cdot)$ on the arc are uniformly small, and concavity along the facet line makes them small on the whole facet, against an auxiliary positive gamble. Otherwise $P_{L_-}>0$ somewhere on the arc; on $F_1$ this contradicts concavity with the zeros at the pinned crossings, and on $F_2$, $F_3$ a strict shell beyond the crossing lies in one strictly signed atom, and a directional face model breaking both atoms the same way violates concavity.
\end{proof}
\status{(a) proved (\src{L1} Thm.~L1.A(a)); confirmed (\src{L1\_referee} \S5), re-derived in full, one reader; it uses neither Lemma~\ref{lem:L17} nor Theorem~\ref{thm:L1C}. (b) on $F_2$, $F_3$ (the middle arcs) proved and confirmed; on $F_1$ proved \emph{modulo} Lemma~\ref{lem:L17}, with two repairs (\src{L1\_referee} \S5): a compactness sentence for the reduction to no inside ties, and the set $\Theta_\tau=\{P^\flat(\cdot,h)\ge0\}$ is not shown closed (not needed) but contains a full neighbourhood of $p^*$, which gives the dichotomy ``$\lambda_\tau\equiv R^*$ or $\lambda_\tau\equiv\lambda\ne R^*$'' directly.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L17z}
Under the standing data, $P^\flat(p^*,\cdot)\equiv0$ on $F_1$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Suppose $P^\flat(p^*,h)<0$ on an open arc $\alpha$ of $F_1$ at $r_{12}$ ($r_{31}$ is symmetric). The inside shell over $\alpha$ lies in $D_{T_1}\setminus D_{K^\flat_{p^*}}\subseteq Z_{p^*}$, is open and connected, and so lies in one atom with normal $b$. If $b_1=0$, the shell lies in $\Lambda\cap(-,-,+)=D_{K_0}\cap O$, so $P_{K_0}\circ h\ge0$ on $\alpha$, and with Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(a) it vanishes there: $\alpha$ is an adjacency arc with non-null inside $\Lambda$-ties, which the first step of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(b) on $F_1$ excludes without Lemma~\ref{lem:L17}. If $b$ is strictly signed, Proposition~\ref{prop:carrying}(c), (d) and the last step of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) run on $F_1$, using Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} only at $e_2$, $e_3$ and crosspin only at the pinned crossings of $F_1$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved in a referee report (\src{L1\_referee} \S4), at the level of the write-up's carrying branch re-read for one weak world; one reader.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:L17}
Under the standing data, for every $\tau\in(0,1)$ the set $A_\tau\coloneqq\{P^\flat(\cdot,h(\tau))>0\}$ on $F_1$ is $\Di$ intersected with an open half-plane whose boundary line $\lambda_\tau$ passes through $p^*$, and $\tau\mapsto\lambda_\tau$ is continuous (steps 1 and 3 of Theorem~\ref{thm:pivot} on $F_1$, for $P^\flat$).
\end{lemma}
\status{CHECKED (\src{L1} Lemma~L1.7), with an explicit dependence on Lemma~\ref{lem:L17z}. \emph{The gap} (\src{L1\_referee} \S4): step~1 applies Lemma~\ref{lem:nopin} on a bracket and needs $p^*$ in its closure; the note assumed $P^\flat(p^*,\cdot)=0$ on all of $F_1$, which fails as written when $p^*\in E$ carries a corner arc of $F_1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:carrying}(b)), and Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(b) on $F_1$ uses Lemma~\ref{lem:L17} at corner points. Lemma~\ref{lem:L17z} closes it. Step~3 is replaced by a direct continuity argument: a jump of the normal would contradict continuity of the concave $\tau\mapsto P^\flat(q,h(\tau))$.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:L1B}
Under the standing data:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\roman*)]
\item the set $\Theta_\Lambda$ of facet rays every conic neighbourhood of which meets $\Lambda$ non-nully is finite: on each facet-orthant arc with $g_1>0$ its points are among the endpoints of the arc, on each arc with $g_1<0$ there is at most one, and the crossings $w_{12}$, $w_{13}$ may be added;
\item near every $h\in\Theta_\Lambda$, $\Lambda$ lies in $E_1(T_1)$: inside $D_{T_1}$ where $g_1<0$, outside where $g_1>0$;
\item every pinned crossing, every corner ray and every point of the $(+,-,-)$-arcs has a neighbourhood in which $\Lambda\subseteq E_1(T_1)$, and the half of a crossing ball on the $T_1$-correct side is strict.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{proved \emph{modulo} Lemma~\ref{lem:L17} (\src{L1} Cor.~L1.B, which says ``proved''; relabelled by \src{L1\_referee} \S5, since (i) needs Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(b) on $F_1$). The sharpening in (i), zeros only at the endpoints of $g_1>0$ arcs, is the referee's.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L1C}
The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a), with Propositions~\ref{prop:crosspin}, \ref{prop:chainchords}, \ref{prop:carrying} and the chain of \S\ref{sec:main}, runs for the standing data. Hence Theorem~\ref{thm:L1}.
\end{theorem}
\status{CHECKED (\src{L1} Thm.~L1.C; one reading, an audit table of every use of strict signs at world~1 and why it survives by Corollary~\ref{cor:L1B}). \src{L1\_referee} \S6: the CHECKED status is justified and the key rows were re-derived. Row~1 (Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_1$) needs one sentence for Lemma~\ref{lem:nopin} at $w_{32}$ and $w_{23}$ with $j=1$: positivity on $[\tau_3-\eta,\tau_3+\eta]$ comes from concavity at the non-exceptional neighbours, which gives the needed containment up to the facet. Row~3 (crosspin at $w_{12}$, $w_{13}$) is simpler with a straddling shell, which contains strict gambles with $g_1<0$ and with $g_1>0$. Row~4 (face models agree with $T_1$ on $\Lambda$) needs its path along $g+s\one$ spelled out. The audit list matches \src{L4}'s independent list (case (II) in part~(b)).}

\emph{Cross-check with configuration (I)} (\src{L1\_referee} \S8). \src{L4}'s (I$_2$) gives, by Lemma~\ref{lem:L46}(c), int-$\Lambda_1$ facet points on the middle arc of $F_2$ near $w_{12}$, which Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(a) excludes, at proved level; (I$_3$) is the mirror. So $P_{K_1}(w_{12})=0=P_{K_0}(w_{13})$, only case (II) remains at an interior $p^*$, and it is closed twice at CHECKED level (part~(b), and Theorem~\ref{thm:L1C}, of which (II) is an instance). Lemma~\ref{lem:L46}(b) is consistent with, and stronger than, \src{L1}'s Lemma L1.5. \src{L4}'s proposed first computation (does the freed coordinate-1 row absorb the box contradiction?) is answered by Proposition~\ref{prop:L12}: yes, algebraically, when both coordinate-1 rows are freed; but Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(a) shows that the freeing configuration cannot occur.

\begin{conjecture}\label{conj:L1D}
No field with ($\gamma_0$), $c\ne0$ a.e., and pairwise-null blind sets $\Lambda_k\coloneqq\{\rho_k=0\}\cap M$ ($\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ null for $i\ne j$) has $D_{T_1}$ as a Bayes model at an interior weight.
\end{conjecture}
\status{conjecture (\src{L1} \S6.3, ``L1.D''); correctly labelled (\src{L1\_referee} \S7). \emph{Necessary conditions} (proved; confirmed): rigidity of $\Lambda_k$ at world~$k$ needs $\Lambda_k\cap(\Lambda_i\cup\Lambda_j)$ null, and on $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ only one coordinate is live. \emph{Gap.} The note's CHECKED claim that its arguments go through verbatim when the closures of the $\Lambda_k$ meet $\partial D_{T_1}$ in pairwise disjoint sets of rays is not justified: a $\Lambda_2$ adjacent along the middle arc of $F_1$ kills Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_2$ there, and the auxiliary set for $\Lambda_1$ on $F_1$ then meets only rays with $\theta$ near $0$. A world-by-world bootstrap is needed (\src{L1\_referee} \S7). By Corollary~\ref{cor:M11p}(a) the pairwise-null hypothesis cannot be dropped. \src{M1} \S2.4 locates the step that does not transfer: crosspin at a pinned crossing of coordinate $c$ when $\Lambda_c$ accumulates there, which Corollary~\ref{cor:L1B} at world $c$ would exclude, but whose proof uses crosspin at the other worlds' pinned crossings. Corollary~\ref{cor:N13}(c) and Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}(b) of part~(f) supply, at the ranking level, the selected between models that the induction would need; it has not been run. Its rigid form is the open question of configuration \cfg{P0} of Theorem~\ref{thm:R21}.}

\paragraph{(e) The $T_1$-shadow, and why the fixed point alone cannot finish (\src{M1}, \src{M1\_referee}).}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M11}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item Let $\rho_k\ge0$ be integrable, with $\rho_k=0$ a.e.\ on $E_k(T_1)\cap M$ and $\rho_k>0$ a.e.\ on $M\setminus E_k(T_1)$ ($k=1,2,3$), and put $c^T\coloneqq(\rho_k\sigma_k)_k$, the \emph{$T_1$-shadow}. Then $c^T\ne0$ a.e.\ on $M$; $B_q=D_{T_1}$ (mod null) for every $q\in\Di$, with null ties; $A(c^T)=\Delta$, so $T_1$ is $c^T$-Bayes at every interior weight, at every point of every open edge and at every vertex; and $d_t(c^T)=0$ for every $t\in\Delta$. Its blind sets are $\Lambda_k=E_k(T_1)\cap M$; $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j=J_l$ is non-null, $\Lambda_1\cap\Lambda_2\cap\Lambda_3=\varnothing$, and each $\Lambda_k$ contains one side of every open facet arc of $D_{T_1}$.
\item For any field $c=(\rho_k\sigma_k)$ with $\rho_k\ge0$, the following are equivalent: $A(c)=\Delta$; $e_1,e_2,e_3\in A(c)$; $\rho_k=0$ a.e.\ on $E_k(T_1)\cap M$ for $k=1,2,3$.
\item The field $(0,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)$ has $\Lambda_1=M$ and $e_1\in A(c)$; each of its $B_q$, $q\in\Di$, is one of $P_2$, $P_3$, $P_2\cap P_3$, so every $B_q$ is coherent, and $d_t=0$ for every $t\in\Delta$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) At $g\in M$ let $C(g)$ be the set of worlds at which $T_1$ is correct; $C(g)\ne\varnothing$ and $C(g)\ne\{1,2,3\}$. For $k\in C(g)$, $\sigma_k(g)=\chi_T(g)$, and for $k\notin C(g)$, $\rho_k=0$; so $q\cdot c^T(g)=\chi_T(g)\sum_{k\in C(g)}q_k\rho_k(g)$, which has the sign of $\chi_T$ for $q\in\Di$ and is $\ge0$ times $\chi_T$ on $\partial\Delta$. (b) $e_k\in A(c)$ iff $\chi_T\rho_k\sigma_k\ge0$ a.e., and $A(c)$ is convex. (c) The sign of $q_2\sigma_2+q_3\sigma_3$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Thm.~M1.1); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S\S1.1--1.2), one reader; NUMERICS.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:M11p}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item There are degenerate fields with three blind sets, $p^*$ anywhere in $\Di$, $c\ne0$ a.e., and every facet arc touched by all three blind sets; so the pairwise-null hypothesis of Conjecture~\ref{conj:L1D} is essential.
\item There are degenerate fields with $p^*$ at a vertex and with $p^*$ on an open edge.
\item $c^T$ satisfies everything Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} extracts from a cover: ($\gamma_0$), $d_t=0$ at every $t\in\Delta$, admissibility, every interior $B_q$ coherent, $c\ne0$ a.e. It satisfies (BU) at every interior weight with $K_q\equiv T_1$, and (TP) at every $p^*$; it fails only the strict-sign clause of Definition~\ref{def:realisation}. So Theorems~\ref{thm:main} and~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) are false for weakly signed fields with $c\ne0$ a.e., and no argument that uses only the countably additive field of the fixed point excludes covers.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Cor.~M1.1$'$); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S1.3), one reader. \emph{Wording repairs.} The note's ``Theorem main and M0closed(a) use strict signs exactly in Lemma UVN'' is false: the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) uses strict signs in four kinds of place (case (II) in part~(b)). The correct statement is: for $c^T$, Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} fails at every vertex ($K_q\equiv T_1$), so the chain already fails at step~0 of Theorem~\ref{thm:pivot}. ``The fixed point alone'' means the countably additive field alone; arguments that use the endorsers themselves, such as Theorem~\ref{thm:M17}, are not covered. The note's headline ``every remaining degenerate case is settled positively at field level'' holds for three blind worlds and for every boundary type, but not for two blind worlds at an interior $p^*$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:M111} excludes the exact-shadow version, and no example is given) or for pairwise-null blind sets (Conjecture~\ref{conj:L1D}, conjectured impossible) (\src{M1\_referee} \S6.4).}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M12}
Assume (OB) with $p^*=e_1$. Then $K_1\cap[e_1,e_2]=\{e_2\}$ and $K_0\cap[e_1,e_3]=\{e_3\}$; $\Lambda_1\supseteq M\cap\{g_1>0\}$, so world~1 is blind on every problem on which it advises acceptance; $\Lambda_1\cap\{g_1<0\}\supseteq D_{T_1}\cap\{g_1<0\}$; and the visible set $V_1=M\setminus\Lambda_1$ lies in $\{g_1<0\}\setminus\cl D_{T_1}$, where $T_1$ rejects and is world-1-correct.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:L43}, $\Lambda_1\supseteq E_1(T_1)\cap M$. On $(-,+,+)\subseteq Q_1\subseteq R_{12}\cap R_{13}$ the world-1 error set of a model is the model, so $D_{K_1},D_{K_0}\supseteq D_{T_1}$ there, and $P_{K_1},P_{K_0}\ge0$ on the closure, which contains $w_{21}=(-1,0,\kappa)$ and $w_{31}=(-1,\kappa,0)$. For $m=(a,1-a,0)$, $m\cdot w_{21}=-a$, and for $m=(a,0,1-a)$, $m\cdot w_{31}=-a$; so $a=0$. Then $D_{K_1}\subseteq P_2$ and $D_{K_0}\subseteq P_3$ reject everything on the $g_1>0$ orthants of $R_{12}$, $R_{13}$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Prop.~M1.2, which states $e_2\in K_1$, $e_3\in K_0$); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S2.1), one reader, who notes the slightly stronger form stated here. NUMERICS. The minimal instance $\Lambda_1=E_1(T_1)\cap M$ is excluded by Proposition~\ref{prop:L47}; every instance of \cfg{V} under (OB) is far from minimal, and Theorem~\ref{thm:M11}(c) shows that the extreme case $\Lambda_1=M$ is consistent at field level.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M110}
Let $c$ have ($\gamma_0$) and $c\ne0$ a.e., fix an edge $\{i,j\}$ with third world $l$, and put $f_\theta\coloneqq\theta\rho_i\sigma_i+(1-\theta)\rho_j\sigma_j$. For a.e.\ $\theta\in(0,1)$ the model equal to $\{f_\theta>0\}$ on $M\setminus(\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j)$ and to $P_l$ on $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ (accepting $N_+$) is coherent, and it equals $P_i$ on $Q_l\setminus(\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j)$. If $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\cap Q_l$ is null, it is $D_K$ with $K\cap[e_i,e_j]\ne\varnothing$ and $K\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_i,e_j])$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p}); for $c^T$ it is $T_1$.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Lemma~M1.10); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S2.2), one reader. It needs every $B_q$ coherent, which holds under ($\gamma_0$) and $c\ne0$ a.e.\ (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(b) with the referee's hypothesis). So the shadow's degeneracy is visible on every edge: its edge limits are $T_1$ itself, not models between two vertices.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M111}
Let $c$ have ($\gamma_0$) and $c\ne0$ a.e., and fix distinct $i,j,k$. If $\Lambda_i=E_i(T_1)\cap M$ (mod null) and $\rho_k>0$ a.e.\ on $J_j\cup J_k$, there is a contradiction.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $q=(1-s,s\eta,s(1-\eta))$ in the coordinates $(i,j,k)$, let $s\to0$ and then $\eta\to0$ along good values. The iterated limit in measure of the coherent $B_q$ is $T_1$ off $J_j$ and the opposite of $T_1$ on $J_j$: it is $Y_j$, which is incoherent (Lemma~\ref{lem:M16}(b)).
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Prop.~M1.11); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S2.3), one reader. \emph{Reading, corrected.} The note's ``a shadow-type degeneracy with exact blind sets needs all three worlds blind, as in $c^T$'' overstates. Applied to $(i,j,k)$ and $(i,k,j)$, the proposition gives only that $\rho_k$ and $\rho_j$ each vanish on a non-null part of $J_j\cup J_k$, on disjoint parts since $c\ne0$; it does not give $\Lambda_j=E_j(T_1)$ or $\Lambda_k=E_k(T_1)$.}

\emph{The ranking level.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M13}
Assume (LA), (S) and strict (G). Let $X\in\M_U$ and $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$. Then some $p$ in the face $\Delta_I$ has $C\coloneqq C_p\preceq_iX$ for every $i\in I$; and if $C\ne X$, then $\mu(E_iX\setminus E_iC)>0$ for every $i\in I$: $C$ fixes some error of $X$ at every world of $I$.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Lemma~M1.3, the face form of Theorem~\ref{thm:kkm}); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S3.1), one reader, including the step ``a model of $\M_U$ is determined by its world-$i$ error set''. Re-proved for edges in \src{N1} \S3.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M14}
Assume (H$_U$), let $\nu_i$ be endorsers at the worlds $i\in I$, let $X$ be regular and $i_0\in I$. If every model $Y$ with $\nu_i(E_iY)\le\nu_i(E_iX)$ for all $i\in I$ has $E_{i_0}X\subseteq E_{i_0}Y$, then $X\in\C_L$, selected on $\Delta_I$.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Lemma~M1.4, from Lemma~\ref{lem:M13}); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S3.2), one reader.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:M15}
Assume (H$_U$), and let the worlds $i\in I$ have countably additive endorsers $\rho_i\mu$.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item For $t\in\Delta$ with $\supp t=I$ and $i_0\in I$, the tie-broken Bayes model $\{\sum_It_i\rho_i\sigma_i>0\}\cup(\{\sum_It_i\rho_i\sigma_i=0\}\cap P_{i_0})\cup N_+$ is coherent and in $\C_L$.
\item For $i\ne j$, with $V_i\coloneqq\{\rho_i>0\}\cap M$, the model equal to $P_i$ on $V_i$ and to $P_j$ on $M\setminus V_i$ is coherent and in $\C_L$; so $(M\setminus V_i)\cap R_{ij}$ is the world-$i$ error set on $R_{ij}$ of a coherent model between $P_i$ and $P_j$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p}).
\item If all three worlds have countably additive endorsers, with $\rho_j,\rho_k>0$ a.e.\ ($j,k\ne i$), then for a.e.\ $\theta$ the vertex-fan model at $e_i$ (equal to $P_i$ on $V_i$ and to $\{\theta\rho_j\sigma_j+(1-\theta)\rho_k\sigma_k>0\}$ off it) is coherent and in $\C_L$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Cor.~M1.5); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S3.3), one reader. \emph{Wording repair.} The note's ``(c) upgrades the `coherent' of Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}(b) to `selected'\,'' holds only when world~$i$'s $\rho_i\mu$ endorses \emph{all} relevant comparisons; in Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}, $\rho_\infty$ endorses only localized comparisons, and in (OB) the density $\rho_1$ is the countably additive part of $\nu^*_1$, which by itself endorses nothing.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M16}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item \emph{Facet-plane lemma.} Let $K\supseteq K'$ be a credal set, $h\in\relint F_m\cap U$ off the crossings, and $N\ni h$ open with $D_K\cap N=D_{T_1}\cap N$ a.e. Then $v_m\in K$.
\item For each $l$, $Y_l$ is incoherent.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Lemma~M1.6, with an open cone $N$ around an arc in (a)); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S3.4), one reader. The local form of (a) stated here is the referee's; it is needed in Corollary~\ref{cor:M19p}. In (b), $Y_3=T_1$ on $Q_1\cup Q_2$, which contains three facet arcs with cones in open orthants (the middle arcs of $F_1$, $F_2$ and the $r_{23}$-corner portion of $F_3$), so $v_1,v_2,v_3\in K$ and $D_K\subseteq D_{T_1}$; but $Y_3=P_1$ on $Q_3$ accepts gambles just outside the middle arc of $F_3$. NUMERICS (midpoint-convexity failures).}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M17}
Assume (LA), (S) and strict (G) on $\M_U$. For each pair $\{i,j\}$, with third world $k$, there are $C\in\C_L$ and non-null $F_i\subseteq E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$, $F_j\subseteq E_j(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$ such that $C$ fixes $T_1$'s world-$i$ errors on $F_i$ and its world-$j$ errors on $F_j$, every endorser $\nu_i$ of world $i$ has $\nu_i(F_i)\ge\nu_i(E_iC\setminus E_iY_k)\ge\nu_i(F_j)$, and every endorser $\nu_j$ of world $j$ has $\nu_j(F_j)\ge\nu_j(F_i)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:M13} to $X=Y_k$, which is regular and incoherent, with $I=\{i,j\}$; then $F_i\coloneqq E_iY_k\setminus E_iC$ and $F_j\coloneqq E_jY_k\setminus E_jC$ are non-null, and $E_i(Y_k)=E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$. On $R_{ij}$ exactly one of $i,j$ is right for any model, so $F_j\subseteq E_iC\setminus E_iY_k$ and $F_i\subseteq E_jC\setminus E_jY_k$. Endorsement of the relevant comparisons $C\preceq_iY_k$, $C\preceq_jY_k$ and finite additivity give the inequalities.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Thm.~M1.7); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S4.1), every line re-derived, one reader. \emph{Scope} (referee). The proof uses only (LA), (S) and strict (G) on $\M_U$, not $T_1\in\C_L$, (C) or (IB), so it holds in \emph{every} such ranking, cover or not. It binds a cover only through blindness: $T_1\in\C_L$ enters through admissibility (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(c), Proposition~\ref{prop:L43}), which makes countably additive parts vanish on $T_1$-error sets. One witness $C$ serves all endorsers simultaneously.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:M18}
In a ranking with (H$_U$), no world $i$ has a countably additive endorser $\rho_i\mu$ with $\rho_i=0$ a.e.\ on $E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$ and $\rho_i>0$ a.e.\ on $E_j(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$, for some $j\ne i$. If the countably additive part of $\nu^*_i$ is positive exactly off $E_i(T_1)$ (the shadow pattern), then every endorser $\nu_i=\rho_i\mu+\pi_i$ has $\pi_i(F_i)\ge\rho_i(F_j)+\pi_i(F_j)$; for $\nu^*_i$ this is positive, so no maximal endorser of world $i$ is countably additive.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{M1} Cor.~M1.8); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S4.2), one reader. The referee gives a second proof through Corollary~\ref{cor:M15}(b), which also shows (\src{M1\_referee} \S4.3; proved in that report): for any world with a countably additive endorser, the blind set on each $R_{ij}$ is the world-$i$ error set of a coherent model between $P_i$ and $P_j$, with no ($\gamma$) and no positivity at the other worlds.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M19}
Assume (H$_U$). Let worlds $i,j$ have countably additive endorsers $\rho_i\mu$, $\rho_j\mu$, and suppose that for some $\theta\in(0,1)$, $\theta\rho_i\ge(1-\theta)\rho_j$ a.e.\ on $R_{ij}\cap E_j(T_1)$ and $(1-\theta)\rho_j>\theta\rho_i$ a.e.\ on $R_{ij}\cap E_i(T_1)$ (or the same with $i$ and $j$ exchanged). Then there is a contradiction. The same holds for arbitrary bounded endorsers $\nu_i$, $\nu_j$ in charge form: if $\theta\nu_i(A)\ge(1-\theta)\nu_j(A)$ for every $A\subseteq E_j(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$ and $(1-\theta)\nu_j(A)>\theta\nu_i(A)$ for every non-null $A\subseteq E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$.
\end{theorem}
\status{The first statement: proved (\src{M1} Thm.~M1.9); confirmed (\src{M1\_referee} \S5.1), one reader. The hypotheses say that $T_1$ agrees on $R_{ij}$ with the tie-broken edge Bayes model, which is then $Y_k$; Corollary~\ref{cor:M15}(a) makes it coherent, against Lemma~\ref{lem:M16}(b). The charge form is proved in a referee report (\src{M1\_referee} \S5.1), one reader, directly from Theorem~\ref{thm:M17}: $\theta\nu_i(F_i)\ge\theta\nu_i(F_j)\ge(1-\theta)\nu_j(F_j)\ge(1-\theta)\nu_j(F_i)>\theta\nu_i(F_i)$. It is the correct arbitrary-endorser version of the first statement.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:M19p}
Assume (H$_U$).
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item If worlds $i,j$ have countably additive endorsers with $\rho_i=0$ on $E_i(T_1)$, $\rho_j=0$ on $E_j(T_1)$ and $\rho_j>0$ a.e.\ on $R_{ij}\cap E_i(T_1)$, there is a contradiction.
\item Let worlds $i$, $j$ have countably additive endorsers of maximal support, and let $I_e\coloneqq\{\theta:\theta e_i+(1-\theta)e_j\in A(c)\}$, a closed interval, be non-empty. If $I_e$ has interior, then $\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$ meets both $E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$ and $E_j(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$ non-nully, each part accumulating at every point of the $R_{ij}$-arcs of some facet ($F_m$ for one side, $F_{m'}$ for the other). If $I_e=\{\theta^*\}$, then on each side the set $\{\rho_i/\rho_j=(1-\theta^*)/\theta^*\}\cup\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$ accumulates at every point of the $R_{ij}$-arcs of some facet, again one facet per side.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{(a) proved (\src{M1} Cor.~M1.9$'$(a)); confirmed, one reader; Corollary~\ref{cor:M18} at world $j$ already suffices. (b) is the referee's replacement (\src{M1\_referee} \S5.2; proved in that report, one reader) of the note's M1.9$'$(b), which claimed ``a two-sided tie shell: a frozen density ratio along every $R_{ij}$-arc of some facet''. What the note proves is accumulation of each side along all $R_{ij}$-arcs of some facet, with the local form of Lemma~\ref{lem:M16}(a); two-sidedness on \emph{one} facet, a frozen ratio (the ties include the joint zero set) and a shell (as opposed to accumulation) are not proved. The note's (c) (admissibility at two vertices leaves only this escape) is correct.}

\emph{What a realisation of the shadow must do} (\src{M1} \S4.1; the requirements are proved necessary, confirmed in \src{M1\_referee} \S6.1).
