A ranking with (H$_U$) whose maximal field is $c^T$ needs, at every world $i$ and for every $j\ne i$: (Sh1) every endorser of world $i$ has countably additive part vanishing on $E_i(T_1)\cap M$, the maximal one positive off it (equivalently, by Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(f), ratio certificates on every non-null subset of $E_i(T_1)$); (Sh2) $\pi^*_i(F_i)\ge\rho^*_i(F_j)>0$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:M18}), so world~$i$ accepts trades giving up countably additive-visible correctness on $F_j$ for fixing parts of its own $T_1$-error set $F_i$ that meet every set of the localizing family of $\nu^*_i$ (``thin pieces'' is not proved); (Sh3) every axiom; (Sh4) the exchanges of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17} on every edge. \emph{The attempts} (descriptions, \src{M1\_referee} \S6.2). Lexicographic worlds with a zero exchange rate on their blind sets have a countably additive endorser of maximal support, (ZER), and are excluded by Corollary~\ref{cor:M18}; one such world on an edge suffices. \src{L2}'s device (part~(g)) is (ZER), with the wrong orientation (blind sources and visible targets, where (Sh2) needs the reverse); it is excluded by Corollary~\ref{cor:M18} only when its blind set is aimed exactly at $E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$. The tilt world of Theorem~\ref{thm:K33} has the right orientation and lacks closed sections. \src{M1} found no closed-section tilt. \emph{Beyond the shadow} (\src{M1} \S4.3; confirmed): with worlds 2, 3 additive with positive densities, $T_1\in\C_L$ forces $\operatorname{ess\,sup}_{J_2}\rho_3/\rho_2\le\operatorname{ess\,inf}_{J_3}\rho_3/\rho_2$, i.e.\ $T_1$ is $(2,3)$-Bayes on $E_1(T_1)\cap R_{23}=J_2\cup J_3$; Lemma~\ref{lem:N25p} below removes the additivity.

\emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{M1}}$} (\src{M1} \S5). Is there a ranking on $\M_U$ with every axiom whose maximal endorser field is the $T_1$-shadow, i.e.\ with $\Lambda_k=E_k(T_1)\cap M$ for every $k$? \emph{Answered: No}, twice and independently (Corollaries~\ref{cor:N13}(a) and~\ref{cor:N26}(a) of part~(f); \src{N12\_referee} \S\S1.3, 2.6). The note's ``equivalently, one in which $T_1$ is admissible at all three vertices'' is not an equivalence: by Theorem~\ref{thm:M11}(b), admissibility at the vertices gives only $\Lambda_k\supseteq E_k(T_1)\cap M$ (\src{M1\_referee} \S6.5); the nearby result for that weaker reading is in Corollary~\ref{cor:N26}. The note's list of what a negative answer would leave is incomplete (two or three blind worlds at an interior $p^*$ with non-null pairwise intersections not of shadow shape, vertex cases with more than one blind world, and the edge case with joint-blindness escapes are also open); the complete list is the configuration list of Theorem~\ref{thm:R21}.

\paragraph{(f) Pareto off the carriers, no blind targets, the swap lemma and the edge dichotomy (\src{N1}, \src{N2}, \src{N12\_referee}).} The tool of this part is that competitiveness can always be tested by partial trades \emph{off the carriers} of the purely finitely additive parts of the endorsers. It needs no closed sections. The two notes overlap on Question~Q$_{\mathrm{M1}}$ and are consistent with each other and with \src{L2} (\src{N12\_referee} \S3, with an exact cell check on \src{L2}'s path).

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N21}
Let $C\in\C_L$ be competitive on $S\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$, $S\ne\varnothing$ (no other axiom is used), and let $\nu_k=\rho_k\mu+\pi_k\in\mathfrak N_k$ for $k\in S$ be any endorsers, $\psi_k(X)\coloneqq\int_{E_kX\cap M}\rho_k\,d\mu$.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item No measurable $W\subseteq M$ has $\psi_k(C\sd W)<\psi_k(C)$ for every $k\in S$.
\item There is $w\in\Delta_S$ with $\sum_{k\in S}w_k\chi_k\rho_k\ge0$ a.e.\ on $M$, where $\chi_k\coloneqq+1$ where $C$ is correct at world $k$ and $-1$ elsewhere: $C$'s advice is pointwise optimal for $w\cdot c$, ties free.
\item If $S=\{i,j\}$ and $C$ is an edge model, then $C$ is $\theta$-Bayes for $(\rho_i,\rho_j)$ with $\theta=w_i$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a) If $W$ improved all $\psi_k$ by $3\eta$, take a set $E$ of small measure carrying all but $\eta$ of $\pi\coloneqq\sum_k\pi_k$ (Step~1 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(b)) and with $\rho_k(E)<\eta$; then $X\coloneqq C\sd(W\setminus E)$ is regular, every $\nu_k$ strictly prefers it, and competitiveness gives some $k$ with $C\preceq_kX$, a relevant comparison that $\nu_k$ would have to endorse. (b) The range of $W\mapsto(\int_W\chi_k\rho_k\,d\mu)_{k\in S}$ is convex and compact (Lyapunov) and misses the open negative orthant; separate. (c) On $R_{ij}$, $\chi_j=-\chi_i$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Thm.~N2.1); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.1), one reader; an elementary proof of (c) without Lyapunov is in the note. \emph{Scope} (referee). The weight $w$ may be a vertex of $\Delta_S$; then the conclusion is only that every world-$i$ error of $C$ lies in $\{\rho_i=0\}$. If $\rho_i\equiv0$ on $R_{ij}$ (a totally countably additive-blind world), every edge model is $1$-Bayes and (c) is vacuous. This is what makes the theorem consistent with \src{L2} and with configuration \cfg{V0}, but every result below that rests on it is empty at a totally blind world. \emph{In \src{M2}'s setting} (\src{N2} Remark~N2.1$'$; confirmed): with world~1 endorsed only by $\varphi\in\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W^{\mathrm f}_1)$ and (RL) partners, (a)--(c) hold for $C=C_q$ with $\supp q\ni1$ and for $C=T_1$, because the off-carrier test model gives a forced pair. So every result below that uses only this theorem on edges $\{1,j\}$ holds there with $\Lambda^\natural$ in place of $\Lambda_1$.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:N22}
Let $C\in\C_L$ be an edge model competitive on $\{i,j\}$, with endorsers $\nu_i$, $\nu_j$.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item If $(R_{ij}\setminus E_iC)\cap\{\rho_i=0<\rho_j\}$ is non-null, then $E_iC\cap R_{ij}\subseteq\{\rho_i=0\}$. Equivalently, if $C$ has a non-null visible world-$i$ error ($E_iC\cap\{\rho_i>0\}$ non-null), then $E_iC\supseteq\{\rho_i=0<\rho_j\}\cap R_{ij}$.
\item Hence no relevant comparison $C\preceq_iX$ with $X$ an edge model has a target $E_iX\setminus E_iC$ that meets $\{\rho_i=0<\rho_j\}$ non-nully together with a source $E_iC\setminus E_iX$ that is not contained in $\{\rho_i=0\}$: a blind target forces a blind source.
\end{enumerate}
The mirror statements hold at world $j$.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Cor.~N2.2); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.2), one reader. By Theorem~\ref{thm:N21}(c), $C$ is $\theta$-Bayes; on the given set $e_\theta=-(1-\theta)\rho_j\ge0$ forces $\theta=1$. No additivity, nestedness or closedness is used. For a blind target the whole trade can be carried by $\pi_i$ on carriers of small measure, but a partial trade off those carriers is also a competitor, seen only by the countably additive parts, and both worlds strictly prefer it; so the obstruction is competitiveness itself, and the closed-choice mechanism of Theorem~\ref{thm:L34} is needed only for visible sources.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:N22p}
Let $C,C'\in\C_L$ be edge models competitive on $\{i,j\}$, $\theta$-Bayes and $\theta'$-Bayes for the same endorser pair. If $\theta<\theta'$, then $E_iC'\cap R_{ij}\subseteq E_iC\cup\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$; if $\theta=\theta'$, they differ only on $\{e_\theta=0\}\cap R_{ij}$. So two members of an edge selection cross only inside the tie sets of the countably additive edge field, and (Nest$_e$) holds on $\{i,j\}$ whenever some endorser pair has $\rho_i,\rho_j>0$ a.e.\ on $R_{ij}$ and $\mu(\{\rho_i=r\rho_j\}\cap R_{ij})=0$ for every $r>0$.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Cor.~N2.2$'$); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.2), one reader. This extends Proposition~\ref{prop:S20}(c) (additive worlds) and the leading-charge case to arbitrary worlds with endorsers.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:N10}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item If $\pi\ge0$ is purely finitely additive on $M$, vanishing on null sets, and $B\subseteq M$ is non-null, some non-null $Q\subseteq B$ has $\pi(Q)=0$.
\item If $C=C_p$ with $\supp p=\{i,j\}$, then $C=P_i=P_j$ a.e.\ on $Q_l\cap M$ ($l$ the third world).
\item For such $C$, $P\subseteq E_iC\cap R_{ij}$ and $Q\subseteq R_{ij}\setminus E_iC$, the \emph{swap} $X\coloneqq C\sd(P\cup Q)$ is regular, and its relevant vectors at $C$ are $\delta_i=1_Q-1_P$ and $\delta_j=1_P-1_Q$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Lemma~N1.0); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.1), one reader.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:N11}
Let $C\in\C_L$ be competitive on $\{i,j\}$ and edge-selected (or $n=2$). Let $\nu\in\mathfrak N_i$, with density $\rho$ and localizing family $\Theta^\nu$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(b)). Suppose $P\subseteq E_iC\cap R_{ij}$ is non-null with $\rho>0$ a.e.\ on $P$, and $Q\subseteq R_{ij}\setminus E_iC$ has $\rho=0$ a.e.\ on $Q$ and $Q\cap\Theta^\nu_m=\varnothing$ for some $m$. Then $\nu_j(Q)=0$ for every $\nu_j\in\mathfrak N_j$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For non-null $P'\subseteq P$ consider the swap $X=C\sd(P'\cup Q)$. If $C\preceq_iX$, the comparison is relevant and $\Theta^\nu$-localized, so Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(b) gives $0=\rho(Q)\ge\rho(P')>0$. So competitiveness gives $C\preceq_jX$, and $\nu_j(Q)\le\nu_j(P'_n)$ for disjoint non-null $P'_n\subseteq P$, $n=1,2,\dots$, whose $\nu_j$-masses sum to at most $1$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Lemma~N1.1); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.1), one reader. In words: a blind target with a visible source is never paid at world $i$ except at its end; off the end, competitiveness must be supplied by world $j$, and shrinking the source makes the target worthless to world $j$ too, purely finitely additive part included. \emph{Correction} (referee): the note's remark that strict (G) enters through Lemma~\ref{lem:N10}(b) is wrong; that lemma is not needed, and no strict (G) is used, only competitiveness and Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(b). \emph{Interior version} (confirmed): for $C=C_p$, $p\in\Di$, and $P$, $Q$ inside $Q_i$, every endorser of some world $l\in\{j,k\}$ vanishes on $Q$.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N23}
Assume (H$_U$). Let $\nu_i\in\mathfrak N_i$ and $\nu_j\in\mathfrak N_j$ have densities with $\mu(\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}\cap R_{ij})=0$. Then for every $\theta\in[0,1]$ both extreme edge Bayes models $E^{\theta,-}$ and $E^{\theta,+}$ lie in $\C_L$; in particular they are coherent.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $X$ be one of them, with world-$i$ error set $A$. Lemma~\ref{lem:M13} on the edge gives $C=C_p\preceq_iX$, $\preceq_jX$; at a vertex $X=C$ by strict (G); at an interior $p$, $C$ is $\theta'$-Bayes (Theorem~\ref{thm:N21}(c)), and since $e_{\theta'}-e_\theta$ has the sign of $\theta'-\theta$ off the null joint blind set, $c\coloneqq E_iC\cap R_{ij}$ satisfies $c\supseteq A$ or $c\subseteq A$. Strict (G) at $i$, respectively at $j$, gives $c=A$, so $X=C$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Thm.~N2.3, from Lemma~\ref{lem:M13} and Theorem~\ref{thm:N21}); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.3), all four inclusions and both vertex cases checked, one reader. The hypothesis is sharp in the proof: without null joint blindness two of the four cases fail. Checked exactly in \src{L2}'s system (\src{n12ref\_py/l2\_consistency.py}).}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:N23p}
Let $\nu^*_i$, $\nu^*_j$ be maximal endorsers with $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\cap R_{ij}$ null. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item the edge models $X_{ij}$ (world-$i$ errors $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}$) and $X_{ji}$ (world-$j$ errors $\Lambda_j\cap R_{ij}$) are in $\C_L$;
\item \emph{rigidity:} $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=E_i(D_K)\cap R_{ij}$ for a coherent $D_K$ with $K\cap[e_i,e_j]\ne\varnothing$ and $K\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_i,e_j])$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p});
\item this is Corollary~\ref{cor:M15}(b), and Corollary~\ref{cor:M15}(a) on edges, without countably additive endorsers, null joint blindness replacing them;
\item every extreme edge Bayes model of the maximal countably additive edge field is coherent at every $\theta\in[0,1]$: an edge form of ($\gamma_0$), for both tie-breakings, at the ranking level.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Cor.~N2.3$'$); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.3), one reader. (b) is Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}(b$'$) at the ranking level, at every world whose blind set its edge partner sees, with no ($\gamma$), (OB) or countably additive endorser.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N12}
Let a ranking on $\M_U$ have strict (G) and (S), and let $i\ne j$ be worlds with (NC). Let $X_\Lambda$ be the edge model whose world-$i$ error set on $R_{ij}$ is $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}$. Then at least one of the following holds.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[(rig)] $X_\Lambda=C_p$ for some $p\in[e_i,e_j]$: $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=E_i(C_p)\cap R_{ij}$ for a selected edge or vertex model, which by Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p} is $D_K$ with $K\cap[e_i,e_j]\ne\varnothing$ and $K\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_i,e_j])$.
\item[(dbl)] There is an edge-selected $C$ such that $\Lambda_i\cap V_j\cap R_{ij}\subseteq E_iC$; $B\coloneqq(\Lambda_i\setminus E_iC)\cap R_{ij}$ is non-null, $B\subseteq\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$, and every endorser of world $j$ vanishes on $B\setminus\Theta^{\nu^*_i}_m$ for every $m$; and $(E_iC\setminus\Lambda_i)\cap R_{ij}$ is non-null.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Thm.~N1.2, by Lemma~\ref{lem:M13} on the edge and Lemma~\ref{lem:N11}); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.2), vertex cases included, one reader. It is the contrapositive of Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}(a), with the extra information on world $j$ in (dbl) (\src{N12\_referee} \S3). Uses (S) through the face KKM lemma and (NC) at $i$ and $j$.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:N13}
Assume (H$_U$).
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item If world $i$ has $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$ and world $j$ has $\rho^*_j>0$ a.e.\ on $E_i(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$, for some $j\ne i$, there is a contradiction. In particular no ranking with (H$_U$) has the $T_1$-shadow as its maximal endorser field: Question~Q$_{\mathrm{M1}}$ has answer No.
\item If an exchange $(C,F_i,F_j)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17} has $F_j\cap V_i$ non-null, then every endorser of world $j$ vanishes on $F_i\cap\Lambda_i\setminus\Theta^{\nu^*_i}_m$ for every $m$, and $F_i\cap\Lambda_i\subseteq\Lambda_j$. So (Sh2) forces $F_i$ to be doubly blind and totally null at world $j$, on a set where $T_1$ is right at $j$.
\item If $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\cap R_{ij}$ is null for all $i\ne j$, then every $\Lambda_i=(E_i(C^{ij})\cap R_{ij})\cup(E_i(C^{ik})\cap R_{ik})$ with \emph{selected} edge or vertex models $C^{ij}$, $C^{ik}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Cor.~N1.3); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.3), one reader. (a): on $R_{ij}$, $E_i(T_1)\cap E_j(T_1)=\varnothing$, so (dbl) fails and (rig) gives $X_\Lambda=Y_k$, incoherent (Lemma~\ref{lem:M16}(b)). This settles Q$_{\mathrm{M1}}$ in the reading $\Lambda_k=E_k(T_1)\cap M$; the weaker reading ``admissible at all three vertices'' is treated in Corollary~\ref{cor:N26}. In (c), (NC) at every world is implicit. So ``fixed point plus the edge dichotomy'' is strictly stronger than the fixed-point route: the shadow passes every field-level test (Corollary~\ref{cor:M11p}(c)) and fails Theorem~\ref{thm:N12} on every edge.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N24}
Assume (H$_U$) and endorsers at $i$ and $j$, and let $(C,F_i,F_j)$ be an exchange of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17}. Then $C=C_p$ with $p$ in the open edge, $C$ is $\theta^*$-Bayes, and exactly one of the following holds:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[(vis)] $\theta^*\in(0,1)$: $F_i\subseteq V_i\cup(\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j)$ with $\theta^*\rho_i\ge(1-\theta^*)\rho_j$ on $F_i$, and $F_j\subseteq V_j\cup(\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j)$ with the reverse inequality;
\item[(int$_i$)] $\theta^*=1$: $E_i(C)\cap R_{ij}\subseteq\Lambda_i$, so the \emph{source} of world $i$'s trade is $i$-blind;
\item[(int$_j$)] $\theta^*=0$: the mirror statement.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Thm.~N2.4, from Theorem~\ref{thm:M17} and Theorem~\ref{thm:N21}); trichotomy confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.4), one reader. \emph{Wording repair.} In (int$_i$) only the source is forced to be $i$-blind; at $\theta^*=1$ the condition on $F_i$ is vacuous, $F_i$ may be visible at $i$, and the inequality $\nu_i(F_i)\ge\nu_i(F_j)=\pi_i(F_j)$ may be carried partly by $\rho_i(F_i)$. The note's ``source and target of world $i$'s trade are both $i$-blind'', ``carried at world $i$ by $\pi_i$ alone'' and ``world $i$ trades errors inside its own blind set against errors inside its own blind set'' hold when $\Lambda_i\supseteq c^{ij}_T$, in particular at $p^*=e_i$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(c)), and so in configuration \cfg{V}.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N25}
Assume (H$_U$) and endorsers at $i$ and $j$, and suppose $c^{ij}_T$ is $\theta_0$-Bayes for $(\rho_i,\rho_j)$. Let $\theta^*$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:N24}. If $\theta^*<\theta_0$, then $F_i\subseteq\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$; if $\theta^*>\theta_0$, then $F_j\subseteq\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$; if $\theta^*=\theta_0$, then $F_i\cup F_j\subseteq Z_{\theta_0}\coloneqq\{e_{\theta_0}=0\}\cap R_{ij}$. Hence:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item if $Z_{\theta_0}$ is null (the joint blind set included), (H$_U$) is contradictory;
\item if the joint blind set on $R_{ij}$ is null, then $\theta^*=\theta_0$, both $Z_{\theta_0}\cap c^{ij}_T$ and $Z_{\theta_0}\setminus c^{ij}_T$ are non-null, and each of them accumulates at every point of every $R_{ij}$-arc of some facet (one facet for each side, possibly different);
\item if the $p^*$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(c), for the same endorser tuple, lies on the closed edge $[e_i,e_j]$, then $c^{ij}_T$ is $\theta_0$-Bayes with $\theta_0=p^*_i/(p^*_i+p^*_j)$; at $p^*=e_i$ the exchanges on both edges at $e_i$ are internal to $\Lambda_i$ or have jointly blind targets.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Thm.~N2.5); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.5), one reader, with two repairs. \emph{(a), wording.} The note calls (a) ``M1.9 for arbitrary endorsers''; that overstates. Theorem~\ref{thm:M19} allows ties, the joint blind set included, on $E_j(T_1)\cap R_{ij}$, whereas (a) needs all of $Z_{\theta_0}$ null; so (a) generalises the endorsers and strengthens the tie hypothesis. The correct arbitrary-endorser version of Theorem~\ref{thm:M19} is its charge form. \emph{(b), gap inherited from the note's M1.9$'$(b).} The note claimed a two-sided tie shell along the $R_{ij}$-arcs of one facet; what is proved is accumulation of each side along every $R_{ij}$-arc of some facet, possibly different facets, using the local form of Lemma~\ref{lem:M16}(a) and Theorem~\ref{thm:N23} for the coherence of $E^{\theta_0,\pm}$ (\src{M1\_referee} \S5.2, \src{N12\_referee} \S2.5). Under null joint blindness the ties are indeed a frozen ratio. In (c) the $p^*$ belongs to the same endorser tuple (referee).}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:N25p}
Assume (H$_U$) and endorsers at $i$ and $j$. There is $\theta_0\in[0,1]$ with $J_j\subseteq\{e_{\theta_0}\le0\}$ and $J_i\subseteq\{e_{\theta_0}\ge0\}$: $T_1$ restricted to $E_k(T_1)\cap R_{ij}=J_i\cup J_j$ is $(i,j)$-Bayes.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Lemma~N2.5$'$); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.5), one reader. $T_1$ is competitive on $\Omega$ (\src{R11} Lemma~IC), and every change on $J_i\cup J_j$ is strictly better at world $k$, so competitiveness passes to $\{i,j\}$; then Theorem~\ref{thm:N21}. This is \src{M1} \S4.3 without additivity.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:N26}
Assume (H$_U$) and (NC) at worlds $i$, $j$. If $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=c^{ij}_T$ (mod null) and $\Lambda_j\cap c^{ij}_T$ is null, there is a contradiction. Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item no ranking with (H$_U$) has the $T_1$-shadow as its maximal field (Question~Q$_{\mathrm{M1}}$: No);
\item in a cover, world $i$ is never blind exactly on $c^{ij}_T$ while world $j$ sees $c^{ij}_T$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:M18} without countably additive endorsers);
\item under (OB), $\Lambda_1=E_1(T_1)\cap M$ gives $X_{12}=Y_3$, a contradiction (Proposition~\ref{prop:L47} at the ranking level, with no ($\gamma$) and no rigidity used);
\item if $T_1$ is admissible at all three vertices for the maximal field ($\Lambda_k\supseteq E_k(T_1)\cap M$ for every $k$), then $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\cap R_{ij}$ is non-null on every edge, and world $j$ is totally null (purely finitely additive part included) on a non-null part of it, off the carrier of $\nu^*_i$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}
\status{The main statement and (a)--(c): proved (\src{N2} Cor.~N2.6); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.6), one reader: the joint blind set is $\Lambda_j\cap c^{ij}_T$, which is null, so Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}(a) puts $X_{ij}=Y_k$ into $\C_L$, against Lemma~\ref{lem:M16}(b). \emph{Wrong statement removed.} The note's (a) continues ``Equivalently (M1.1(b)), no cover has $T_1$ admissible at all three vertices''. That is not proved and is not an equivalence: three-vertex admissibility of the maximal field means $\Lambda_k\supseteq E_k(T_1)\cap M$, not equality, and an enlarged $\Lambda_j$ can make $\Lambda_j\cap c^{ij}_T$ non-null (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.6, repeating \src{M1\_referee} \S6.5). (d) is the nearby result that is proved (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.6, proved in that report from Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p} and the main statement, one reader): if the joint blind set were null on $R_{ij}$, then $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=c^{ij}_T$ and $\Lambda_j\cap c^{ij}_T=\varnothing$; the last clause is Theorem~\ref{thm:N12}(dbl). The note's item (d), there called ``M1.11 at the ranking level'', is its ranking-level analogue and not Proposition~\ref{prop:M111}: neither hypothesis implies the other.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N27}
Assume (H$_U$) on $\M_U$ and (NC) at every world (or, in (d), the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:M26}). There is no cover in any of the following cases.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item \emph{One-sided exact shadow:} on some edge, $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=c^{ij}_T$ and $\Lambda_j\cap c^{ij}_T$ is null (Corollary~\ref{cor:N26}); this includes the $T_1$-shadow.
\item \emph{Tie-free edge-Bayes target:} on some edge, $c^{ij}_T$ is $\theta$-Bayes for $(\rho^*_i,\rho^*_j)$ with $Z_\theta$ null (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(a)); in particular when $p^*$ lies on the closed edge and the edge field has no ties at $\theta_0$.
\item \emph{Boundary target weight without accumulation:} $p^*$ lies in the open edge $(e_i,e_j)$, the joint blind set on $R_{ij}$ is null, and for one side ($Z_{\theta_0}\cap c^{ij}_T$ or $Z_{\theta_0}\setminus c^{ij}_T$) accumulation fails along the $R_{ij}$-arcs of every facet (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(b), (c)).
\item \emph{The vertex configuration with a refined veto:} worlds~2 and~3 add up and world~1 satisfies (NC) (or the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:M26}), so that \cfg{V} holds; $V_1$ is non-null; and world~1 refines its countably additive veto $\Phi_1(X)\coloneqq\int_{X\cap V_1}\rho^*_1\,d\mu$, i.e.\ $\Phi_1(X)<\Phi_1(Y)$ implies $X\prec_1Y$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{N2} Thm.~N2.7); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S\S2.5, 2.7), one reader. (c) is stated in the referee's one-sided form; the note's two-sided form inherited the gap of Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(b). (d) verified in full by the referee: by Proposition~\ref{prop:M12}, $V_1\subseteq\{g_1<0\}\setminus\cl D_{T_1}$, so $\Phi_1$ charges only world-1-wrong acceptances and is a veto in the sense of Theorem~\ref{thm:L34}; (Pay) holds, $\Phi_1(P_j)=\rho^*_1(V_1\cap R_{1j})>0$ for some $j$; and (Imp) holds by Corollary~\ref{cor:N22}(a): a selected edge model with $\Phi_1(C_q)>0$ errs on all of $\Lambda_1\cap R_{1j}\supseteq M\cap\{g_1>0\}\cap R_{1j}$, and fixing a piece of it is $\Phi_1$-neutral and strictly better at world~1. So Theorem~\ref{thm:L34} forbids closed choice on $[e_1,e_j]$. \emph{Hypotheses still needed:} (NC) at the two worlds of the edge, or the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:M26}; strongly (M1) worlds next to non-(RL) partners remain outside. Edge results never exclude (vis) exchanges, which strictly positive fields have; those are excluded only globally, by Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a). The note's ``$T_1$ is not edge-Bayes on $R_{ij}$ for $p^*\in\Di$'' is an unproved reading.}

\emph{Nested edges} (\src{N1} \S4). Setting: either $n=2$ with $\C_L$ a chain, $R\coloneqq M$, $i=1$; or $n=3$, an edge $\{i,j\}$ with (Nest$_e$), $R\coloneqq R_{ij}$.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:N14}
Index the edge selection by the chain itself: $c_t$, $t\in[0,1]$, with $\mu(c_t)=t\mu(R)$, as in \src{P4B\_referee} Lemma~N0. Then: (a) for $\tau\in(0,1]$, $c_\tau=\bigcup_{s<\tau}c_s$, and for $\tau\in[0,1)$, $c_\tau=\bigcap_{s>\tau}c_s$ (mod null); (b) for $t\in[0,1)$ and non-null $D\subseteq R\setminus c_t$, some $t'\in(t,1)$ has $C_{t'}\preceq_i C_t\sd D$.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Lemma~N1.4) after the referee's repair; confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.4), including $\tau=1$ and $\tau=0$, one reader. \emph{Repair.} The note indexed by the edge prior and said that ``by (Nest), $c_t$ is nondecreasing''. That does not follow: (Nest) says only that $\{E_i(C):C\in\C_L\}$ is a chain, and Lemma~N0 gives continuity and surjectivity of $p\mapsto\mu(E_1C_p)$, not monotonicity of $p\mapsto c_p$. Indexing by the chain, Lemma~N0(iii) gives closed sections and N0(iv) competitiveness on $\{i,j\}$ at every interior index, and the proofs run verbatim.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N15}
In the setting above, let $\nu\in\mathfrak N_i$ with density $\rho$. Then $\{\rho=0\}\cap R=c_g$ (mod null) for some $g\in[0,1]$. No hypothesis is placed on world $j$ beyond the axioms.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Thm.~N1.5); confirmed after the repair of Lemma~\ref{lem:N14} (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.5), steps 1--3 re-derived, one reader. Strict escape gives a relevant, $\Theta^\nu$-localized comparison that makes the slab just right of a cut blind, and no-jump continuity carries the blindness to the left end. This is strictly more than Proposition~\ref{prop:K38}, which needed an additive partner.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:N16}
In the setting above: (a) if a relevant comparison $C_t\preceq_iX$ has a target meeting $\{\rho=0\}$ non-nully, its source lies in $\{\rho=0\}$; so no relevant comparison has a blind target and a visible source; (b) every $\Lambda_\Theta$ and $\Lambda_\infty$ is an initial segment of the chain, for every partner (Proposition~\ref{prop:K38} for every partner); (c) the shape is attained, for every cut, in \src{L2}'s full system (part~(g)), with \src{L2}'s orientation, blind sources and visible targets; (d) on a (Nest$_e$) edge, if $F_i\cap\Lambda_i$ is non-null then $F_j\subseteq\Lambda_i$, so an exchange of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17} there is between visible pieces or between two blind pieces.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Cor.~N1.6); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.5), one reader. A two-world full system with blind targets therefore needs a non-nested $\C_L$: a rigid or tied crossing, both worlds failing (MC$_{\mathrm{sel}}$) along it, and its blind target totally null at the partner (Lemma~\ref{lem:N11}), hence in alternative (dbl). This is a list of necessary conditions (\src{N1} \S4, confirmed); none of these crossings has been inhabited.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:N17}
Let a ranking on $\M_U$ satisfy (Sh1), (Sh2) on some edge $\{i,j\}$, and let world $j$ be visible a.e.\ on $c^{ij}_T$ (as in $c^T$). Then (S) fails: for the exchange witness $C$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17}, a non-null $Q\subseteq F_i$ off the carrier of $\nu^*_i$ and a small non-null $P'\subseteq F_j\cap V_i$ with $\pi^*_j(P')=0$, the swap $C\sd(P'\cup Q)$ has $C\not\preceq_iX$ and $C\not\preceq_jX$.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{N1} Thm.~N1.7, from Lemma~\ref{lem:N11}); confirmed (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.7), one reader. So gluing three blind-target edge systems into a shadow-like cover breaks at competitiveness of one edge witness against one swap, before closedness, (C) or (LF) are reached, and wherever the end of world $i$ is placed.}

\begin{conjecture}\label{conj:N1C}
Every coherent model $D_K$ between $P_i$ and $P_j$ with $K\cap(e_i,e_j)\ne\varnothing$ (that is, $K$ meets the \emph{open} edge) crosses $T_1$ on $R_{ij}$: both $(E_i(T_1)\setminus E_iD_K)\cap R_{ij}$ and $(E_iD_K\setminus E_i(T_1))\cap R_{ij}$ are non-null.
\end{conjecture}
\status{conjecture; \src{N12\_referee} \S1.8's restriction of \src{N1}'s Conjecture N1.C. \emph{N1.C as stated is false.} It asserted the crossing for every coherent between model other than $P_i$, $P_j$. Counterexample (\src{N12\_referee} \S1.8, $i=1$, $j=2$): take $q\in T_1\cap\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_2])$ with $q\notin\co(K'\cup\{e_1\})$, for instance $q=(v_1+v_2)/2$ at $(\varepsilon,s)=(0.3,0.5)$ or $(0.6,0.5)$, and $K\coloneqq\co(K'\cup\{e_1,q\})$, so $D_K=P_1\cap\{q\cdot g>0\}$. Then $K\cap[e_1,e_2]\ni e_1$ and $K\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_1,e_2])$, so $D_K$ is a between model; it is not $P_1$ (separation of $q$ from $\co(K'\cup\{e_1\})$ gives an open set of $g\in R_{12}$ with $g_1>0>q\cdot g$), and not $P_2$ ($D_K\subseteq P_1$). Its world-1 errors on $R_{12}$ are the $g$ with $g_1>0$ and $q\cdot g\le0$, which $D_{T_1}$ also rejects since $q\in T_1$: so $E_1D_K\cap R_{12}\subseteq E_1(T_1)\cap R_{12}$ and $D_K$ does not cross $T_1$ (NUMERICS confirm; the note's script never tested $K$ containing a vertex). With $K$ meeting the open edge every sampled model crossed $T_1$, the smaller crossing piece decaying like $O(t)$ as the edge point tends to $e_i$ (NUMERICS). \emph{Consequence, restricted.} If the conjecture holds, then under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:N13}(a) Lemma~\ref{lem:N11} forbids every edge-selected model $D_K$ with $K$ meeting the open edge. Open-edge-selected models can have $K\cap[e_i,e_j]$ at a vertex (Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p} gives only $K\cap[e_i,e_j]\ne\varnothing$), so even then not every intermediate edge-selected model is covered.}

\emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$} (\src{N1} \S7; field level; open). Is there a field $c=(\rho_k\sigma_k)$ on $M$, $\rho_k\ge0$ integrable, with ($\gamma_0$); $B_q$ coherent for $q\in\Di$ whenever $c\ne0$ a.e.; $T_1$ $c$-$p^*$-Bayes for some $p^*\in\Delta$; at least one non-null $\Lambda_k$; and, for every ordered pair $(i,j)$, either $\Lambda_i\cap R_{ij}=E_i(D_K)\cap R_{ij}$ for a coherent between model $D_K$, or $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\cap R_{ij}$ non-null? \emph{No} excludes every cover in which all three worlds satisfy (NC) (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}, Theorem~\ref{thm:N12} with Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p}, and Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(d) for the case where every $\Lambda_k$ is null), so that $T_1$ on $\M_U$ would reduce to covers with a world \emph{failing (NC)} (the note's ``with an (M1) world'' is corrected by the referee: (M1) worlds with (NC) are inside the question, and next to two (RL) partners so are worlds failing it, Theorem~\ref{thm:M26}). \emph{Yes} gives the shape a construction must realise: rigid edge segments of \src{L2}'s shape, or doubly blind overlaps. The shadow $c^T$ has every property except the edge alternative, so Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$ strictly sharpens what the fixed-point route left (Corollary~\ref{cor:M11p}(c)). The referee recommends two strengthenings, each proved: replace the rigid alternative by Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}(d) (whenever the joint blind set on $R_{ij}$ is null, every extreme edge Bayes model of $(\rho^*_i,\rho^*_j)$ is coherent), and add to the doubly blind alternative the partner-nullness of Theorem~\ref{thm:N12}(dbl), which is not field-level but constrains any realisation. Its restrictions to the configurations of Theorem~\ref{thm:R21} are the open questions of \cfg{PD}, \cfg{E} and \cfg{X}.

\paragraph{(g) Blind-set constructions (\src{L2}, \src{L23\_referee}).} Setting as for Theorem~\ref{thm:D21}: $n=2$, $K'=[\alpha',\beta']\subseteq(0,1)$, $U=D_{K'}$, $\lambda\coloneqq\mu/\mu(M)$, the path $C_b$ ($b\in[0,1]$) of \src{C2} Thm.~C2.1 reindexed so that $c_b\coloneqq E_1C_b\cap M=\{x<b\}$ for a chain coordinate $x$ pushing $\lambda|_M$ to Lebesgue measure, $d_b\coloneqq M\setminus c_b$, selection $p\mapsto C_{p_2}$, $\tau_f(t)\coloneqq\int_{M\cap\{x\ge t\}}f\,d\lambda$ and $D(\delta)\coloneqq\int_{N_+}\delta\,d\lambda$. \emph{The design.} Fix $a\in(0,1)$ and $u_0\in(a,1)$; blocks $B_k\coloneqq M\cap\{u_k\le x<u_{k+1}\}$ with $u_k\coloneqq1-(1-u_0)5^{-k}$ accumulate geometrically at $x=1$; $\mathrm{ref}_k$ is the left $4/5$ of $B_k$. Level $n$ uses finitely many blocks, indexed by the points of a projective plane PG$(2,q_n)$ with $q_n\ge4^n$ prime, and its generators trade a thin strip of $c_a$ for $\bigcup_{k\in\ell}\mathrm{ref}_k$ along lines $\ell$. The base cone is tail dominance, $\{f:\tau_f\ge0\text{ on }[0,1]\}$. World~1 rejects a vector $\delta$ with $D(\delta)<0$, accepts one with $D(\delta)>0$, and, when $D(\delta)=0$, accepts $\delta$ iff it vanishes on $N_+$ and its restriction to $M$ lies in the base cone translated by a sum of at most one generator per level. Two same-level targets share a block, because two lines of a projective plane meet, and everything to the right of that block has measure less than twice the shared part; so sums of two same-level generators are blocked by measure alone. World~2 is additive with density~1.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L21}
For every $K'$ and every $a\in(0,1)$ the ranking just described, with selection $p\mapsto C_{p_2}$, satisfies strict (G), (IB), (LA), (S) (competitiveness on $\supp p$ and closed sections for \emph{every} evaluable model at both worlds), (C), $\C_L=\{C_b:b\in[0,1]\}$, and (LF) at every interior $C_b$.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{L2} Thm.~L2.1, with Lemmas L2.2 and L2.3); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S\S A.1--A.3), one reader; NUMERICS (exact rationals, two levels). Closed world-1 sections come from compactness of the space of selectors (one generator per level), with no finiteness condition such as \src{D2}'s (D3). Accepting every vector with $D(\delta)>0$ is harmless: such models are dominated and touch no relevant comparison.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L24}
In the system of Theorem~\ref{thm:L21}: (a) for every localizing family $\Theta$ and every $\nu\in\mathfrak N(\mathfrak W_\Theta)$ at world~1, $\nu(c_a)=0$; (b) $\lambda|_{d_a}/(1-a)$ is a countably additive endorser of every relevant world-1 comparison; (c) hence (NC) holds, $\Lambda_\Theta=\Lambda_\varnothing=\Lambda_\infty=c_a=E_1(C_a)$ for every $\Theta$, $a_\infty=a$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:K38}), world~1 is in mode (M2) and is not (Loc$_{\mathrm{int}}$). So Conjecture~\ref{conj:K3C} is false, and Question~Q$_{\mathrm{K3}}$ has answer Yes in a full two-world system next to an additive world.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{L2} Thm.~L2.4); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S A.4), one reader. In (a), each level-$n$ generator can be moved off any set of small measure inside its blocks, and averaging the level-$n$ comparisons gives a certificate $\le\varepsilon_n-1_{c_a}$ with $\varepsilon_n\le4\cdot2^{-n}$, made of $\Theta$-localized relevant comparisons. The referee notes that $\neg$(M0) follows directly from (a), and $\neg$(M1) from Proposition~\ref{prop:L25}, with no appeal to \src{N17} Lemma~3.1. Consistent with Theorem~\ref{thm:F14}, whose export step never triggers here; this also confirms that Theorem~\ref{thm:F14} does not reach chain-free certificates whose positions tend to the end (\src{K3\_referee} \S8). The blind set has the rigid shape of Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}(b$'$) on the edge: the world-1 error set of a selected coherent model between $P_1$ and $P_2$.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L25}
With the gap blocks between levels chosen suitably, world~1 of Theorem~\ref{thm:L21} is endorsed, in the cancellation form, by $\rho\coloneqq\varphi\circ x$ for a nondecreasing $\varphi:[0,1)\to(0,\infty)$ with $\int^1\varphi=\infty$, with no localization at all. So world~1 is (Loc) with a $\sigma$-finite density, it lies in (Loc)$\setminus$(Loc$_{\mathrm{int}}$), and it is not in (N).
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{L2} Prop.~L2.5); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S A.5), one reader. This realises the observation of \src{K3\_referee} \S1.4 that (N) may be strictly smaller than $\{\Lambda_\infty\text{ non-null}\}$, but the example is not in (N).}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:L26}
(a) The strong classification of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31} (every world that does not add up is in mode (M1) or (Loc$_{\mathrm{int}}$)) is false in a full system, already for $n=2$ next to an additive world. (b) The weak classification ((N) empty) is not touched. (c) For $T_1$: under (H$_U$), next to two worlds with integrable densities endorsing all their relevant comparisons, a world of class (Loc) is impossible (Theorem~\ref{thm:H12}); so the mechanism of Theorem~\ref{thm:L21}, which produces (Loc) worlds, cannot supply the exceptional world of Theorem~\ref{thm:K37}, and a non-localizable blind set aimed at $T_1$ next to integrable partners must come with $\neg$(Loc), i.e.\ with world~1 in (N).
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{L2} Cor.~L2.6); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S A.6), one reader.}

\begin{conjecture}\label{conj:L2C}
In the setting of Proposition~\ref{prop:K38} (two worlds, world~2 additive with integrable density, every axiom), every world that is not in mode (M1) is (Loc) with a $\sigma$-finite endorser; i.e.\ (N) is empty there.
\end{conjecture}
\status{conjecture (\src{L2} L2.C), with heuristic evidence only; properly labelled (\src{L23\_referee}).}

\emph{Three worlds} (\src{L2} \S7; not constructed, an analysis). A lift must contain every comparison that competitiveness forces at world~1, keep blocking and strictness, have closed world-1 sections in the 2-simplex, and satisfy (C). The two-world blocking argument fails at forced trades out of a block into the thin tie wedges $\{|p_2\rho_2\sigma_2+p_3\rho_3\sigma_3|<p_1\rho_1\}$ of $R_{23}$; with a large common factor near the $e_1$ ray in $(+,-,-)$ these leaks can be made smaller than the blocks, but proving blocking needs a separating endorser of the whole forced cone, which was not found. \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{L2}}$} (open): on $\M_U$ with worlds 2, 3 additive, is there a coherent selection and a non-null $O$ near the $e_1$ ray in $(+,-,-)$ such that the forced cone of world~1 contains no $f$ with $f\le-1$ on $O$ and $f\le1$ elsewhere? By Corollary~\ref{cor:L26}(c) such a lift would still be (Loc); its $T_1$-aimed form is the question of configuration \cfg{V+} of Theorem~\ref{thm:R21}. \emph{Consistency with part~(f)} (\src{N12\_referee} \S3, exact cell check): \src{L2} is nested with $\Lambda=c_a$ of the shape of Theorem~\ref{thm:N15} and Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}(b); its path is $1$-Bayes for $b<a$ and $\tfrac12$-Bayes for $b>a$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:N21}(c)); every $E^{\theta,\pm}$ is a path model (Theorem~\ref{thm:N23}); and its comparisons have blind sources and visible targets (Corollaries~\ref{cor:N16}(c), \ref{cor:N22}). Its world~1 does not refine its countably additive veto $\lambda|_{d_a}$: that veto is paid at $e_2$, (Imp) holds by Corollary~\ref{cor:N22} (a selected $C_b$ with visible errors has $b>a$ and contains $c_a$, and fixing a piece of $c_a$ is neutral), and the system has closed sections, so Theorem~\ref{thm:L34} forbids refinement (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.8; the proof is this, not anything in \src{L2}).

\paragraph{(h) The VB near-cover, and vetoes cannot be paid (\src{L3}, \src{L23\_referee}).} \src{BRIEF17} proposed two strategies: an ordinal limit of gauge covers converging to $T_1$, and two-grade worlds on two-sided domains. Both end at one theorem.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L31}
(a) Let a ranking on a decomposable domain that is two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$ satisfy strict (G), (S) and (LA), with (LF) at $T_1$ and $T_1\in\C_L$. Then $C_{e_i}=\{g:g_i>0\}$ a.e.\ for every $i$; in particular acceptance is in the advice range of a.e.\ $g$ that is not $\le0$, so a.e.\ mixed pair has both acceptances in its advice range (property (Av) of part~(i)). (b) Every gauge mixture of \src{R10a} on such a domain has $M_i\subseteq\R_+e_i$, so its covered targets are normalised boxes. (c) $c(\varepsilon)\coloneqq\inf_{\text{boxes}}d_{\mathrm H}(\nu(\text{box}),T_1)>0$.
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{L3} Prop.~L3.1); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S B.1), one reader. (a) uses \src{R10a} Thm.~V and Cor.~V2, which hold for any ranking with these hypotheses; it is the ranking-level form of the result of \S\ref{sec:general-N28} that, in every additive cover, the advice range of a.e.\ mixed pair contains both acceptances. \emph{NUMERICS corrected.} The note's minima $0.0080$, $0.0375$, $0.0314$, $0.0168$ ($\varepsilon=0.05,0.3,0.6,0.9$) are not minima; the referee's search gives the upper bounds $c(\varepsilon)\le0.0068$, $0.029$, $0.031$, $0.011$, with numerically symmetric optimal boxes. Positivity is proved and unaffected. So on two-sided domains there is no sequence of gauge covers converging to $T_1$; the gauge polygons of \src{R10a} Prop.~M$'$ live on one-sided domains.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L32}
Fix $K'$ with $u\in K'\subseteq\relint T_1$, $U=D_{K'}$. For $0<a<b$ the gauges $M_i\coloneqq\co\{ae_i,bK',bv_i\}$ form a compatible gauge tuple with domain $U$, so a full additive system on $\M_U$ covering $D_{K_p}$, $K_p=\nu(\sum_ip_iM_i)$, at every interior $p$ with (LF); and $d_{\mathrm H}(K_u,T_1)\le C(\varepsilon,K')\,a/b$.
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{L3} Prop.~L3.2); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S B.2), one reader; NUMERICS. So the degeneration of gauge covers is not a loss of (LF) margin, as \src{BRIEF17} supposed, but a separation of scales inside the gauges: at stage $(a,b)$, $f_i(h)=\min(ah_i,\ b\min_{K'}k\cdot h,\ b\,v_i\cdot h)$.}

\emph{The veto--Brier rankings.} On $\M_U$, with $v_i\cdot h=(1-\varepsilon)u\cdot h+\varepsilon h_i$, put $V^{\mathrm{veto}}_i\coloneqq\{v_i\cdot h<0\}$, $\Phi_i(X)\coloneqq\int_{X\cap V^{\mathrm{veto}}_i}|v_i\cdot h|\,d\mu$ (a \emph{veto}: it charges only $i$-wrong acceptances), $\Psi_i(X)\coloneqq\int_{E_i(X)}|h_i|\,d\mu$ and $\tilde\Psi_i(X)\coloneqq\int_{E_i(X)\setminus V^{\mathrm{veto}}_i}|h_i|\,d\mu$. \textbf{VB} ranks world $i$ by $(\Phi_i,\Psi_i)$ lexicographically, and \textbf{VB$'$} by $(\Phi_i,\tilde\Psi_i)$. The selection is $C_p\coloneqq U\cap\{p\cdot h>0\}\cap\bigcap_{m\in\supp p}\{v_m\cdot h\ge0\}=D_{K_p}$, $K_p=\co(K'\cup\{p\}\cup\{v_m:m\in\supp p\})$; so $K_p=\co(T_1\cup\{p\})$ for interior $p$, and $C_{e_j}=U\cap\{h_j>0\}$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L33}
(a) VB$'$ is the lexicographic limit of the systems of Proposition~\ref{prop:L32} as $a/b\to0$; along any non-principal ultrafilter the limit orders refine $(\Phi,\tilde\Psi)$-lex; VB refines the leading scale $\Phi$; and the selection is the Hausdorff limit of the stage Bayes families at every $p\in\Delta$. (b) VB and VB$'$ satisfy strict (G), (IB), (LA), (LF) at $T_1$ and (C); every $C_p$ is coherent, competitive on $\supp p$ and undominated, for every $p\in\Delta$; and $C_p=T_1$ for every $p\in T_1$, so $T_1\in\C_L$ with a plateau. (c) Every section $\{p:C_p\preceq_mX\}$ is closed relative to $\Di$, and on an open edge the sections of the two worlds of the edge are closed; for $X\coloneqq C_{e_j}\setminus A$, with $A$ a non-null proper part of $C_{e_j}\cap V^{\mathrm{veto}}_i$, the world-$i$ section contains $\Di$ but not $e_j$. (d) No world of VB or VB$'$ adds up.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{L3} Thm.~L3.3), with the referee's repairs; confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S\S B.3--B.4), one reader. \emph{Repair of (a)} (GAP, fixable). The note claimed that VB itself is the lexicographic limit. On the deep veto set $\{v_i\cdot h<(a/b)h_i\}$ the stage gauge is exactly $b\,v_i\cdot h$, with no $ah_i$ term, so the stage loss is $b\Phi_i+a\tilde\Psi_i+o(a)$, not $b\Phi_i+a\Psi_i+o(a)$; two models that differ only on the deep veto set, with equal $\Phi_i$ and different $\int|h_i|$, are tied at every stage but strictly ordered by VB (NUMERICS: $\max|f_i-b\,v_i\cdot h|=0$ on the deep veto sample). So (a) holds for VB$'$, and VB refines the leading scale, which is the sense of ``ordinal limit'' used in Theorem~\ref{thm:L35}. The referee re-ran (b)--(d) for VB$'$: models with $\Phi_m=0$ accept nothing in $V^{\mathrm{veto}}_m$, so $\tilde\Psi_m=\Psi_m$ on them, and the vector-uniqueness argument for (C) goes through. \emph{Repair of (c)} (WRONG clause removed). The note's ``closed relative to each open edge'' is false for the world $k$ off the edge: on $(e_i,e_j)$, $\Phi_k(C_{q_t})>0$ varies with $t$, and a model $C_{q_{t_0}}$ minus a $\Phi_k$-neutral world-$k$-wrong piece has a world-$k$ section containing $q_t$ for $t\uparrow t_0$ but not $q_{t_0}$ (NUMERICS). The headline stands: the failures are at boundary priors. (b) answers the question left open in \src{P3} \S4 (``everything except (Cl)''), with the boundary members checked. NUMERICS (empirical measure; checks the pointwise and lexicographic algebra only).}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L34}
Take any ranking on any decomposable domain with strict (G), and a selection $p\mapsto C_p$; let $B^m$ be the world-$m$-best model, so that $C_{e_m}=B^m$ under competitiveness at $e_m$. Let world $i$ \emph{refine a veto} $\Phi(X)=\int\omega(g,a_X(g))\,d\mu$, with $\omega\ge0$, $\omega(g,a)=0$ unless $a$ is $i$-wrong at $g$, and $\Phi(B^i)=0$: $\Phi(X)<\Phi(Y)$ implies $X\prec_iY$. Let $j\ne i$, and assume:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[(Pay)] $\Phi(B^j)>0$;
\item[(Imp)] every selected $C_q$, $q\in[e_i,e_j]$, with $\Phi(C_q)>0$ has a model $Z$ with $\Phi(Z)=\Phi(C_q)$ and $Z\prec_iC_q$.
\end{itemize}
Then no selection is competitive on $\supp q$ for every $q\in[e_i,e_j]$ with closed sections at worlds $i$ and $j$. No (IB), (C), totality or third world is used, and the target plays no role.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Put $f(t)\coloneqq\Phi(C_{q_t})$ along $q_t=(1-t)e_i+te_j$. Splices of $B^i$ and $B^j$ realise every value in $[0,\Phi(B^j)]$, so refinement and closedness at $i$ make $f$ lower semicontinuous below $\Phi(B^j)$. Off the set $T$ of $t$ at which $C_{q_t}$ agrees with $B^j$ on the paid region, a small move towards $B^j$ is strictly better at $j$; closedness at $j$ and competitiveness on $\{i,j\}$ make $f$ upper semicontinuous there. So $f$ is continuous from $f(0)=0$ up to the first point of $T$, where $f\ge\Phi(B^j)$. At the first $t_c$ with $f(t_c)=\Phi(B^j)/2$, the model $Z$ of (Imp) satisfies $C_{q_t}\preceq_iZ$ for $t\uparrow t_c$, and closedness at $i$ gives $C_{q_{t_c}}\preceq_iZ$, against $Z\prec_iC_{q_{t_c}}$.
\end{proof}
\status{proved (\src{L3} Thm.~L3.4); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S B.5), each step checked, one reader. The last step is the mechanism of \src{R2} Thm.~7 (improvable undominated models take only countably many values); the new input is that closed choice and edge competitiveness \emph{produce} the needed continuum of values as soon as a vertex model pays a veto. \emph{Application to VB} (confirmed): (Pay) holds because $B^j$ accepts the non-null set of gambles just beyond the middle arc of $F_i$; (Imp) holds because a coherent $C=D_K$ with $\Phi_i(C)>0$ has $e_i\notin K$, hence $e_i\notin\co(K\cup T_1)$, and removing a piece of the open set of $h$ with $h_i<0$ positive on $K\cup T_1$ is $\Phi_i$-neutral and strictly better. So VB's preorders admit no selection whatever with closed sections, and Theorem~\ref{thm:L33}(c) cannot be repaired by changing the selection. \emph{Remark} (\src{L23\_referee} \S B.6): on $\M_U$, where silence is in the advice range of every pair, (Imp) holds under strict (G) for every ranking whose veto vanishes on $\cl D_{T_1}$; so ``keep the veto but break (Imp)'' is closed there.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:L35}
Let gauge systems $(M_{i,n})$ on a common decomposable domain with (LF) at $T_1$ have targets $K_{u,n}\to T_1$, normalise by $s_n\coloneqq\max_i\max_{M_{i,n}}|m|$, and let $f_{i,n}/s_n\to f^\infty_i=\min_{M^\infty_i}m\cdot h$ along a subsequence ($M^\infty_i$ a Blaschke limit), with (N$_\infty$): $f^\infty\not\equiv0$ on the set of orientations whose acceptance is in the advice range. Let an ordinal limit be an order refining the leading scale that has strict (G) at the worlds concerned (for instance an ultrafilter limit, or a lexicographic limit with a strictly guiding tail). Then $f^\infty_i\le0$, $f^\infty_i=0$ on $\cl D_{T_1}$, the leading level of the limit is a pure veto, some vertex model pays it, (Imp) holds, and by Theorem~\ref{thm:L34} the limit preorders admit no selection with closed sections.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{L3} Thm.~L3.5, there with (N) for (N$_\infty$)); confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S B.7), one reader, with two hypotheses made explicit: the Blaschke limit is along a subsequence, and the ordinal limit must have strict (G) at worlds $i$ and $j$ (it does not follow from ``any order that refines the leading scale''). The argument is \src{R10a} Thm.~R with weak signs. \emph{What a repair must do} (CHECKED in the note, not independently verified): its vetoing world cannot refine the limit's leading level; the sentence ``a repair must give up refining the leading level'' is supported by Theorem~\ref{thm:L34} and the remark above, and ``near the boundary of $\Delta$'' is interpretive. Without (N$_\infty$), the theorem is a conjecture (\src{L3} \S6).}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:L36}
On a two-sided domain, let world $i$ depend, compatibly with (IB), only on a wrong-advice charge $W_i$ and a silence charge $S_i$, both positive on non-null sets, and assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a).
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item If world $i$ is total, its order on value differences is a half-plane with inner normal $a\ge0$, $a\ne0$: $a\propto(0,1)$ (silence first) violates (G); $a\propto(1,0)$ is the \emph{wrong-first} world, which refines the full veto $W_i$; $a>0$ gives a world that adds up.
\item A wrong-first world never certifies $T_1$ against the model $R''$ equal to $T_1$ except for silence on the mixed pairs of $N\cap D_{T_1}$ ($N$ the (LF) neighbourhood); so a cover has at most two wrong-first worlds. Theorem~\ref{thm:L34} applies to a wrong-first world with (Pay) automatic, and (Imp) holds at every selected model that is not precise; so such a world is compatible with closed choice only if the edge selection is precise on an uncountable set of edge priors.
\item For unanimities over a set $A_i$ of directions in the closed quadrant: if $(1,0)\in A_i$, world $i$ never certifies $T_1$ against $R''$; if $(0,1)\in A_i$, never against the precise model $D_{p^*}$, which is never silent on a two-sided domain; otherwise world $i$ adds up.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{L3} Prop.~L3.6), with the referee's repair; confirmed (\src{L23\_referee} \S B.8), one reader. \emph{Repair.} The note used the regular vacuous model $R$, silent on every mixed pair, and said that by Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a) every mixed pair has all three advices in its advice range. Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a) gives both acceptances only; silence is guaranteed only on the (LF) neighbourhood $N$, so $R$ need not be evaluable. The referee's $R''$ is evaluable by (LF), and $T_1$ is $m$-wrong on a non-null part of $N\cap D_{T_1}$ near $F_m$, so $W_m(R'')<W_m(T_1)$ at every world and the conclusions follow. The half-plane step of (a) is written out by the referee. \emph{Precise-edge residual} of (b): a correct reduction; that it is empty is a CONJECTURE. \emph{Adding-up two-grade worlds} fall under Theorem~\ref{thm:D1}'s open branch ($p^*\notin E\ne\varnothing$); the note's claim that the routes of Theorem~\ref{thm:gm} break there at exactly one input is a survey assertion, CHECKED at most. The note's remark that dropping boundary priors from (S) ``trivialises coverage'' is reworded (referee): interior-only (S) admits lexicographic systems such as VB and constant selections.}

\emph{Nearby result} (\src{L3} \S0, as corrected). On $\M_U$, $T_1$ is covered by a lexicographic ranking under every requirement except closed sections at boundary priors (VB or VB$'$, Theorem~\ref{thm:L33}); closed choice fails exactly where the veto must be paid (Theorem~\ref{thm:L34}). So the boundary of $\Delta$ is where closed choice carries content against lexicographic structure.

\paragraph{(i) The two-sided extension (\src{M3}, \src{M23\_referee}).} \emph{Ladders.} On a decomposable domain $\M$ let $A(g)$ be the advice range of $g$ (Remark~\ref{rem:advicerange}) and $A'(g)\coloneqq A(g)\setminus\{\times\}$. For a.e.\ mixed $g$ and each world $k$ the advices in $A'(g)$ have distinct world-$k$ background ranks $r_k(g,a)\in\{0,\dots,|A'(g)|-1\}$. The \emph{ladder} of world $k$ is $\mathrm{Ld}_k\coloneqq\{(g,j):g\in M,\ 1\le j\le|A'(g)|-1\}$ with $\mu\otimes$counting measure, and the \emph{ladder profile} of a model $X$ is $\lambda_k(X)(g,j)\coloneqq1[r_k(g,a_X(g))\ge j]$. On a pair with advice range $\{+,0,-\}$ there are two steps: step~1 (the model is not correct; the \emph{silence step}) and step~2 (it accepts the world-$k$-wrong orientation; the \emph{wrong step}). On a general domain a model is called \emph{regular} if it is correct on a.e.\ unanimous pair and gives contradictory advice ($\times$) on a null set only (a definition; it shrinks $\mathfrak W_k$, which only weakens (NC)). (NC), endorsers and $\mathfrak N_k$ are defined as before, with ladder vectors $\lambda_k(X)-\lambda_k(B)$ of relevant comparisons $B\preceq_kX$ and charges on $\mathrm{Ld}_k$. For an endorser $\nu=\rho_\nu(\mu\otimes\#)+\pi_\nu$, the \emph{ladder field} has penalty $\ell^\nu_k(g,a)\coloneqq\sum_{j\le r_k(g,a)}\rho_\nu(g,j)$; on a $\{+,0,-\}$ pair write $r^{\mathrm s}_k\coloneqq\rho(g,1)$ and $r^{\mathrm w}_k\coloneqq\rho(g,2)$. The ladder field is strictly guiding iff every ladder density is positive a.e. \textbf{(Av)}: a.e.\ mixed pair has both acceptances in its advice range. By Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a), (Av) holds for every ranking with strict (G), (S), (LA), (LF) at $T_1$ and $T_1\in\C_L$ on a domain that is two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$. On $\M_U$ it fails.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M30}
(a) Two regular models with the same ladder profile at world $k$ agree a.e. (b) Strict (G) at $k$ says exactly that $\lambda_k(X)\le\lambda_k(Y)$ a.e.\ implies $X\preceq_kY$, strictly if the inequality is strict on a non-null set. (c) Theorem~\ref{thm:K31} holds verbatim on $(\mathrm{Ld}_k,\mu\otimes\#)$: endorsers exist iff (NC); purely finitely additive parts localize; there is a canonical blind set $\Lambda_k\subseteq\mathrm{Ld}_k$; and if world $k$ adds up in the general sense of \src{B2} (a bounded strictly guiding loss and a weight positive on non-null sets of pairs with non-singleton advice range, endorsing all relevant comparisons), then $\Lambda_k$ is null.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Lemma~M3.0, Thm.~M3.1); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.1), one reader. The proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:K31} uses only a finite measure space and bounded functions.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M32}
(a) An endorser of world $k$ is a charge on its ladder, i.e.\ on $\{+,0,-\}$ pairs a pair of charges $(\nu^{\mathrm s}_k,\nu^{\mathrm w}_k)$ on $M$; one charge on graded errors is the special case $\nu^{\mathrm w}=\nu^{\mathrm s}$. Endorsers need not be graded; and if some $B\in\C_L$ is silent at world $k$ on a non-null set $A_0$ of two-sided pairs on which $r^{\mathrm w}>r^{\mathrm s}$ on a non-null part, no graded endorser is positive on that part. (b) At every fixed point of Theorem~\ref{thm:M34} (degenerate or not), $\sum_kp^*_k(r^{\mathrm w}_k-r^{\mathrm s}_k)\ge0$ a.e.\ on $T_1$'s silent two-sided pairs; if the field is strictly guiding with ($\gamma$) and $D_{T_1}$ Bayes at $p^*\in\Di$, the inequality is strict.
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Prop.~M3.2), with the referee's repairs; one reader. \emph{(a).} The structural claim is confirmed. The note's ``nothing in the axioms reduces the pair to one graded charge'' was asserted without a witness (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.2): the weak reading has a one-line witness (an additive world with ladder densities $r^{\mathrm s}\ne r^{\mathrm w}$ on a non-null set, whose own ladder charge is an ungraded endorser; such systems satisfy the axioms at the status of Theorem~\ref{thm:ccibu}), and the strong reading holds only in the restricted form stated, which is proved in that report (no argument is known for the case $r^{\mathrm w}<r^{\mathrm s}$). \emph{(b).} The strict form, from the exclusion of triple (apex) ties at $p^*$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:B21}; \src{B2} B2.1(d)), is confirmed, but on (Av)-domains it is vacuous, because Theorem~\ref{thm:M310} leaves no non-degenerate fixed point; the weak form at every fixed point is the non-vacuous remnant, proved by the same two lines in \src{M23\_referee} \S6.2. With $\nu^{\mathrm w}=\nu^{\mathrm s}$ the silence cell collapses to a line, so every interior Bayes model of a single graded charge is precise.}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M34}
Let $\M\ni D_{T_1}$ be a decomposable domain, and let a ranking on $\M$ satisfy strict (G), (IB), (LA), (S) with closed sections, (C), $T_1\in\C_L$ and (NC) at every world. For every endorser tuple $\nu$:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=(\alph*)]
\item for every regular $X$ some $C\in\C_L$ has $C\preceq_kX$ and $\nu_k(\lambda_kC)\le\nu_k(\lambda_kX)$ at every $k$; so $\mathrm{Gap}_t(\nu)=0$ at every $t\in\Delta$;
\item ($\gamma_0$): at every $t\in\Delta$, boundary and exceptional weights included, some coherent model of $\M$ is $\psi^\nu$-$t$-Bayes; if $\psi^\nu$ is strictly guiding, ($\gamma$) holds and the directional families and the strict-Bayes model at every $q\in\Di$ are coherent;
\item $D_{T_1}$ is $\psi^\nu$-$p^*$-Bayes for some $p^*\in\Delta$;
\item if $p^*$ lies in an open edge $(e_i,e_j)$, then on every non-null set of pairs where $T_1$'s advice is wrong at both $i$ and $j$, $\rho_i$ and $\rho_j$ vanish on every ladder step separating $T_1$'s advice from an advice in the range correct at both; if $p^*=e_i$, the same holds for world $i$ alone on all of $T_1$'s world-$i$ errors; in particular, if $\psi^\nu$ is strictly guiding, $p^*\in\Di$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Thm.~M3.4, with the absorption Lemma~M3.3); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S\S6.3--6.4), all four items, one reader. This is Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} on every decomposable domain. (LF) supplies silence in the advice range near the boundary, which with strict guidance gives $p^*\in\Di$.}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:M35}
(a) \emph{Claim B2.0 holds.} Under strict (G), (IB), (LA), (S), (C), $T_1\in\C_L$ and (M0) in the general sense, on any decomposable domain, every supporting assessment $\psi$ satisfies ($\alpha^*$) at an interior weight, ($\beta$) at every weight, ($\gamma$) and ($\delta$). (b) Consequently Corollary~\ref{cor:D17} holds at the status of Theorem~\ref{thm:D1}, and Corollary~\ref{cor:B22} is no longer conditional on Claim~B2.0. (c) The analogues of Propositions~\ref{prop:L44} and~\ref{prop:L45} hold on the ladder.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Cor.~M3.5); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.5), one reader, which closes \src{B2\_referee}'s documentation gap on Claim B2.0. \emph{Documentation repair} (referee): (a) needs the identification of the supporting assessment with the ladder field of the weight of Lemma~\ref{lem:M30}(c): the two differ by a function of $g$ alone, so they have the same Bayes models, ties and exceptional set. Imports: Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}, Lemma~\ref{lem:H11} and Theorem~\ref{thm:kkm}, each read once or more. Corollary~\ref{cor:D17} needs only ($\alpha^*$), ($\gamma$) and $\rho>0$ (\src{D1\_referee} \S8).}

\emph{Theorem~\ref{thm:gm} and the fixed-point field} (\src{M3} \S4; confirmed as an analysis, \src{M23\_referee} \S6.6). The fixed-point field has integral penalties with an integrable envelope, satisfies Proposition~\ref{prop:necessary}(b)--(d), and is strictly guiding iff non-degenerate; it satisfies Proposition~\ref{prop:necessary}(a) (an a.e.-unique Bayes model at every interior weight) iff $E(\psi)=\varnothing$. So if $E\ne\varnothing$, Theorem~\ref{thm:D1} gives $p^*\notin E$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:gm} does not apply as it stands; the claim that the routes of Theorem~\ref{thm:gm} use the axioms only through Proposition~\ref{prop:necessary} is CHECKED, not re-verified, and not load-bearing.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M36}
Let $\psi$ be a strictly guiding integral ($\gamma$)-field on $\M$ with (LF) at $D_{T_1}$, and let $D_{T_1}$ be its a.e.-unique Bayes model at $p^*\in\Di$ ($p^*\notin E$). There are balls $B_2\subseteq B_1$ around $p^*$ such that: (a) every $q$-Bayes model with $q$ near $p^*$ is close to $D_{T_1}$ in measure; (b) every coherent $q$-Bayes model with $q\in B_1$ has credal set close to $T_1$ and containing a fixed compact $K''\subseteq\operatorname{int}T_1$; (c) for a.e.\ pair with an orientation $h$ in the cone over the compact collar $N_0$ of \S\ref{sec:general}, rejection of $h$ (acceptance of $-h$) is weakly optimal at no $q\in B_1$, and the only possible tie is accept-versus-silence on $\{c(h)\cdot q=0\}$; (d) for $q\in B_2$ every non-null tie set consists of such near-facet pairs, frozen along their chords inside $B_2$; (e) set-type tie rules that are coherent on $B_2$ are quasi-linear at near-facet levels.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Lemma~M3.6); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.7), (a)--(e), one reader. Step~3 of (c) is stronger than stated: the closed reject cell of $h$ is empty or the closure of the open one. So inside $B_2$ a two-sided field, restricted to near-facet pairs, is a field of $U$-domain type at every weight and for every tie rule, and chords accumulating at $p^*$ are handled by the $U$-domain audit of Proposition~\ref{prop:chainchords}.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M37}
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:M36}: (a) for good $g$ and every convex tie-breaking family the acceptance set of $g$ lies between the open chart and its closure, with equality off $E$, and for the strict-Bayes family everywhere; (b) $q\mapsto K_q$ is Hausdorff-continuous at every $q\notin E$; (c) one-sided chart facts hold at $q\notin E$; (d) under (Av), limits of $K_q$ at an edge prior lie in that edge, and $K_q\to\{e_b\}$ as $q\to e_b$.
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Lemma~M3.7); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.8), one reader; the third item of (c) rests on the CHECKED transfer of \src{R4} Thm.~B off $E$ (an import from \src{D1}), and Proposition~\ref{prop:M38} does not use it.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M38}
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:M36}, assume (Av), and assume that (TS), (PC), (NS) of Theorem~\ref{thm:TS} hold at $p^*$ together with its unique-cluster clause. Then there is a contradiction (route~I1 of \S\ref{sec:gm-I1}, run with priors off $E$ only).
\end{proposition}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Prop.~M3.8; transfer written out); confirmed (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.9), every replacement checked, one reader. The every-$q$ chart form is replaced by Lemma~\ref{lem:M37}(a)--(c), edge confinement by Lemma~\ref{lem:M37}(d), and pinned chart lines carry no atoms.}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:M39}
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:M36}, with (Av): (TS) holds, and the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:TS} hold on a ball around $p^*$; hence the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:M38} hold.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:M310}
Let $\M$ be a decomposable domain with (LF) at $D_{T_1}$ and (Av), and let a ranking on $\M$ satisfy strict (G), (IB), (LA), (S) with closed sections for every model, (C), $T_1\in\C_L$ and (NC) at every world. Then for every endorser tuple some world's ladder density vanishes on a non-null subset of its ladder; equivalently, some canonical ladder blind set is non-null.
\end{theorem}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Thm.~M3.10) except Proposition~\ref{prop:M39}, which is CHECKED with the fixable gap (ii); Lemmas~\ref{lem:M36}, \ref{lem:M37} and Proposition~\ref{prop:M38} are read once (\src{M23\_referee}); \src{D1} is read once, with repairs (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.11). The logic: strict guidance gives ($\gamma$) and $p^*\in\Di$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:M34}); Theorem~\ref{thm:D1} gives $p^*\notin E$; Propositions~\ref{prop:M39} and~\ref{prop:M38} give a contradiction ($E=\varnothing$ included). (Av) holds on every domain two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a), now refereed once (the note still said ``not yet refereed'').}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:M310p}
On every decomposable domain with (LF) and (Av), in particular on every domain two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$, no ranking with strict (G), (IB), (LA), (S), (C) and $T_1\in\C_L$ has every world adding up. Every cover there needs a world with a non-null ladder blind set, or a strongly (M1) world.
\end{corollary}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Cor.~M3.10$'$, through Corollary~\ref{cor:M35}) at the status of Theorem~\ref{thm:M310}: CHECKED at Proposition~\ref{prop:M39}, pending its gap (ii). This is case (M0) on these domains, closed as on $\M_U$, and it answers \src{D1}'s conjecture of its \S4 there.}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:M311}
Assume (Av). At a vertex $e_k$, on a $\{+,0,-\}$ pair the world-$k$ ladder losses of correct acceptance, silence and wrong acceptance are $0$, $r^{\mathrm s}_k$ and $r^{\mathrm s}_k+r^{\mathrm w}_k$. So vertex ties at $e_k$ occur exactly where the ladder step adjacent to the correct advice is blind, and wrong acceptance is optimal at $e_k$ only where every step is blind. If moreover $\Lambda^{\mathrm s}_k\cap\Lambda^{\mathrm w}_k$ is null and no step of a $\{+,-\}$ pair is blind (where $\Lambda^{\mathrm s}_k$, $\Lambda^{\mathrm w}_k$ are the pairs on which the silence step, resp.\ the wrong step, is blind), then: the directional vertex limits at $e_k$ differ from the precise model $D_{\{e_k\}}$ only on $\Lambda^{\mathrm s}_k$; Lemma~\ref{lem:UVN} at $e_k$ can fail only on pairs of $\Lambda^{\mathrm s}_k$; and every coherent vertex-fan model $D_K$ has $e_k\in K$ and $\Lambda^{\mathrm s}_k\supseteq\{g:g_k>0,\ P_K(g)<0\}$ (mod null).
\end{lemma}
\status{proved (\src{M3} Lemma~M3.11) in the form restated by the referee; one reader. \emph{Gap repaired} (\src{M23\_referee} \S6.12). The note's ``wrong-blindness never creates a tie at a vertex'' is false on $\Lambda^{\mathrm s}_k\cap\Lambda^{\mathrm w}_k$ (all three advices cost $0$) and on $\{+,-\}$ pairs, so its consequence $e_k\in K$ fails if a fan model accepts a world-$k$-wrong orientation on a non-null doubly blind set; the extra hypothesis is added. The referee sees no way to prove it from Theorem~\ref{thm:M34}(d), which constrains blindness only on joint $T_1$-error sets. So on (Av)-domains the vertex template of configuration (I) of part~(b) is reproduced by silence-blindness; wrong-blindness is a different degeneracy, constrained at interior $p^*$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:M32}(b). The full wrong-first world is Proposition~\ref{prop:L36}(b), whose (b) is repaired as stated there.}
