\paragraph{(j) The reduction theorem (\src{R21}).} \src{R21} (round 21) is an integrator's note: it assembles the results of parts~(a)--(i) into one case analysis, adds no assumption, and proves only four short elementary inferences of its own, each marked below as \emph{proved in \src{R21}, unrefereed}. When \src{R21} was written the inputs from \src{N1} and \src{N2} were unrefereed; they have since been refereed once (\src{N12\_referee}), and the statuses below are updated accordingly, with the repairs of part~(f).

\emph{In words.} In every cover each world either has an endorser or has none. If some world has none, the cover is in configuration \cfg{S}, unless both partners have leading densities, in which case Theorem~\ref{thm:M26} pushes it to \cfg{V}. If every world has an endorser, the maximal endorsers give one countably additive field, and that field makes $T_1$ a Bayes model at some weight. If the field is strictly signed, Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) kills the cover, so some world is blind on a non-null set. One blind world forces the target weight to its vertex: configuration \cfg{V}, in two kinds, \cfg{V0} and \cfg{V+}. Two or more blind worlds give four configurations, \cfg{P0}, \cfg{PD}, \cfg{E}, \cfg{X}, split by where the target weight can sit and by whether blind sets overlap. Each configuration has one open question. On other decomposable domains with (LF), the two-sided extension of part~(i) gives the same first cuts.

\emph{Case variables} (Part A). (NC) at each world. (RL) at each world (it implies (NC); \src{R21}). When every world satisfies (NC): a maximal endorser tuple $\nu^*$ and its field $c^*$; the blind sets $\Lambda_k$, which do not depend on the choice of $\nu^*$; the number $b$ of non-null $\Lambda_k$; and $A^*\coloneqq A(c^*)$, which is non-empty (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(c)), closed and convex, with the choice-free \emph{vertex criterion} $e_k\in A^*$ iff $\Lambda_k\supseteq E_k(T_1)\cap M$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:M11}(b)). \emph{Location trichotomy} (proved in \src{R21}, unrefereed; elementary: a convex subset of $\partial\Delta$ lies in one closed edge): exactly one of \cfg{int} ($A^*\cap\Di\ne\varnothing$), \cfg{edge} ($A^*\subseteq[e_i,e_j]$ and $A^*$ meets the open edge $(e_i,e_j)$), \cfg{vtx} ($A^*=\{e_i\}$) holds. Part B uses (NC) on the ladder, the maximal ladder field of Theorem~\ref{thm:M34}, and (Av).

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:R21}
\emph{Part A (the $U$-domain).} Let a ranking satisfy (H$_U$) on $\M_U$. Then exactly one of the following configurations occurs, and every other branch of the case analysis is contradictory.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[\cfg{S}] Some world fails (NC), and some partner of a world that fails (NC) fails (RL). (This includes the case of two or more worlds failing (NC).)
\item[\cfg{V0}] One blind world at its vertex, totally blind. Either (origin I) every world satisfies (NC), $b=1$ with $\Lambda_1$ non-null, and $A^*=\{e_1\}$; or (origin II) world~1 fails (NC), worlds~2 and~3 satisfy (RL), and $\Lambda_1\coloneqq\Lambda^\natural$ is the blind set of the forced endorser of Lemma~\ref{lem:M21}(c). In both cases $V_1=M\setminus\Lambda_1$ is null.
\item[\cfg{V+}] The same, with $V_1$ non-null.
\item[\cfg{P0}] Every world satisfies (NC), $b\ge2$, $A^*\cap\Di\ne\varnothing$, and $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ is null for all $i\ne j$.
\item[\cfg{PD}] Every world satisfies (NC), $b\ge2$, $A^*\cap\Di\ne\varnothing$, and $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ is non-null for some $i\ne j$.
\item[\cfg{E}] Every world satisfies (NC), and $A^*\subseteq[e_i,e_j]$ meets the open edge $(e_i,e_j)$.
\item[\cfg{X}] Every world satisfies (NC), $A^*=\{e_i\}$, and some $\Lambda_j$, $j\ne i$, is non-null.
\end{itemize}
Within the branch in which every world satisfies (NC), the configuration depends on the choice of $\nu^*$ only through the location of $A^*$ when $A^*$ is not a vertex.

\emph{Part B (other domains).} Let $\M\ne\M_U$ be a decomposable domain with (LF) at $D_{T_1}$, and let a ranking satisfy (H$_U$) with $\M_U$ replaced by $\M$. Then exactly one of the following configurations occurs.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[\cfg{GS}] Some world fails (NC) on its ladder.
\item[\cfg{GL}] (Av) holds, every world satisfies (NC) on its ladder, and the maximal ladder field is degenerate.
\item[\cfg{GnAv-nd}] (Av) fails, every world satisfies (NC) on its ladder, and the maximal ladder field is non-degenerate.
\item[\cfg{GnAv-d}] (Av) fails, every world satisfies (NC) on its ladder, and the maximal ladder field is degenerate.
\end{itemize}
The remaining branch \cfg{G0} ((Av), (NC) on the ladders, non-degenerate maximal ladder field) is contradictory, at the status stated below.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch: the case tree]
\emph{Part A, node 0:} (NC) at every world? \emph{Node II} (no). (II-a) If exactly one world fails (NC), say world~1, and worlds~2 and~3 satisfy (RL), Theorem~\ref{thm:M26} gives a contradiction or $p^*=e_1$ with $\Lambda^\natural\supsetneq E_1(T_1)\cap M$: configuration \cfg{V}, origin II, split by $V_1$ into \cfg{V0} and \cfg{V+}. (II-b) Otherwise some partner of a failing world fails (RL), since (RL) implies (NC): configuration \cfg{S}. \emph{Node I} (yes). Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} applied to $\nu^*$ gives $c^*$ with ($\gamma_0$) and $A^*\ne\varnothing$. (I.0) $b=0$: $c^*$ is strictly signed, and Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(d) gives a contradiction. (I.1) $b=1$, with $\Lambda_1$ non-null. Location \cfg{edge} would need two blind worlds on $J_l$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:L43}). Location \cfg{vtx} at $e_j$, $j\ne1$, would need $\Lambda_j\supseteq E_j(T_1)\cap M$, but $\Lambda_j$ is null. Location \cfg{int}: for $p^*\in A^*\cap\Di$, (OB) holds with $\rho^*_2,\rho^*_3>0$; Theorem~\ref{thm:L49} leaves (I$_2$), (I$_3$) or (II); (I) is impossible by Proposition~\ref{prop:L4R} and, independently, by Theorem~\ref{thm:L1A}(a); (II) is excluded at CHECKED level, twice (part~(b) and Theorem~\ref{thm:L1C}). Location \cfg{vtx} at $e_1$: configuration \cfg{V}, origin I, split by $V_1$. (I.2) $b\ge2$: by the location trichotomy, \cfg{int} with all $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ null is \cfg{P0}; \cfg{int} with some overlap is \cfg{PD}; \cfg{edge} is \cfg{E}; \cfg{vtx} is \cfg{X}. \emph{Exclusivity.} The branches are separated by the (NC) pattern, by $b$, by the location trichotomy, by the overlap test and by the nullity of $V_1$; the two origins of \cfg{V} are separated by the (NC) pattern; $b$, the $\Lambda_k$ and the vertex case do not depend on the choice of $\nu^*$. \emph{Exhaustiveness.} Every node has exhaustive exits.

\emph{Part B, node 0:} (NC) on every ladder? If not: \cfg{GS}. If so, Theorem~\ref{thm:M34} gives the maximal ladder field, with ($\gamma_0$) and $T_1$ Bayes at some $p^*$. \emph{Node A:} (Av)? (If $\M$ is two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$, (Av) holds by Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a).) With (Av), a non-degenerate field is branch \cfg{G0}, contradictory by Theorem~\ref{thm:M310} (Theorem~\ref{thm:D1} gives $p^*\notin E$, then Propositions~\ref{prop:M39} and~\ref{prop:M38}); a degenerate one is \cfg{GL}. Without (Av), $\M$ is not two-sided near $\partial D_{T_1}$, and the field is non-degenerate (\cfg{GnAv-nd}) or degenerate (\cfg{GnAv-d}).
\end{proof}
\status{The theorem is as strong as its weakest input on the route to each configuration (\src{R21} \S2). \emph{That each configuration exists as a branch} rests only on refereed inputs and the elementary inferences of \src{R21}: Theorem~\ref{thm:K31}(a)--(c), Theorems~\ref{thm:L41} and~\ref{thm:M11}(b), Proposition~\ref{prop:L43} (refereed once each), Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a) (refereed twice), Theorem~\ref{thm:M26} (its sharp form proved in a referee report), and, for Part~B, Theorem~\ref{thm:M34} and Proposition~\ref{prop:L31}(a) (refereed once). \emph{The closed branches:} I.0 at the status of Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} and Theorem~\ref{thm:M0closed}(a); I.1(\cfg{int}) only at CHECKED level, because of case (II) (upgrading it needs the source proofs listed in item (d) of the audit in part~(b)); I.1(\cfg{edge}) and I.1(\cfg{vtx} at $e_j$) at the status of Proposition~\ref{prop:L43} and Theorem~\ref{thm:M11}(b); \cfg{G0} at CHECKED level, pending gap (ii) of Proposition~\ref{prop:M39}. \emph{The structure items} listed below for each configuration carry the statuses given there; those that rest on \src{N1} and \src{N2} were unrefereed in \src{R21} and are now refereed once (\src{N12\_referee}). The weakest inputs on each route are: for \cfg{V0} and \cfg{V+}, case (II) (CHECKED); for \cfg{P0} and \cfg{PD}, Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} and Theorem~\ref{thm:N12}/Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p} (refereed once); for \cfg{G0}, Proposition~\ref{prop:M39} (CHECKED, with a fixable gap). The inference ``(RL) implies (NC)'', the location trichotomy, the interval statement in \cfg{E} and the remark in \cfg{GL} are proved in \src{R21} and unrefereed; the last is only a sketch.}

\emph{The configurations on $\M_U$: structure, the open question, and what each answer does.}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \cfg{S}: a world failing (NC) next to a partner that is not (RL). \emph{Structure:} almost none. If every world satisfies (NC) for the family $\mathfrak D_k\cup\mathfrak T_k$, the fixed point of Theorem~\ref{thm:L41} still exists (Proposition~\ref{prop:M27}); the edge tools of part~(f) need (NC) and do not apply; no full system with a world failing (NC) is known. \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm S}$} (the first part of \src{M2}'s Q$_{\mathrm{M2}}$, sharpened by Theorem~\ref{thm:M26}): is there a full system on $\M_U$ ($n=3$, every axiom, closed sections for every model, (C); $T_1\in\C_L$ not required) with a world failing (NC), one of whose partners fails (RL)? \emph{No} closes \cfg{S}; \emph{Yes} does not realise it.
\item \cfg{V} (\cfg{V0}, \cfg{V+}): one blind world, $p^*$ at its vertex. Worlds~2 and~3 add up ($\rho^*_2,\rho^*_3>0$ a.e.). \emph{Structure:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item[(V1)] $A^*=\{e_1\}$; $\Lambda_1\supsetneq E_1(T_1)\cap M$; $\Lambda_1\supseteq(M\cap\{g_1>0\})\cup(D_{T_1}\cap\{g_1<0\})$; $V_1\subseteq\{g_1<0\}\setminus\cl D_{T_1}$, where $T_1$ rejects and is world-1-correct (Corollary~\ref{cor:L4V}, proved in a referee report; Proposition~\ref{prop:L47} and Corollary~\ref{cor:N26}(c); Proposition~\ref{prop:M12}; refereed once).
\item[(V2)] The edge models with world-1 errors $\Lambda_1\cap R_{12}$ and $\Lambda_1\cap R_{13}$ are $D_{K_1}$ and $D_{K_0}$, and they are selected, with $K_1\cap[e_1,e_2]=\{e_2\}$ and $K_0\cap[e_1,e_3]=\{e_3\}$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}, with its input Lemma~\ref{lem:M13}; Proposition~\ref{prop:M12}; refereed once).
\item[(V3)] Every edge-selected model on $[e_1,e_j]$ has world-1 errors $c\subseteq\Lambda_1\cap R_{1j}$ or $c\supseteq\Lambda_1\cap R_{1j}$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:N22}; refereed once).
\item[(V4)] The exchange of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17} on $[e_1,e_j]$ is internal to $\Lambda_1$: type (int$_1$), with both pieces in $\Lambda_1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:N24}, Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(c) with $\theta_0=1$; refereed once; the wording repair of Theorem~\ref{thm:N24} does not affect this case).
\item[(V5)] $T_1$ is $(2,3)$-Bayes on $J_2\cup J_3$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:N25p}; refereed once).
\item[] Under (Nest$_e$) on $\{1,j\}$, $\Lambda_1\cap R_{1j}$ is an initial segment of the edge chain (Theorem~\ref{thm:N15}, refereed once after the repair of Lemma~\ref{lem:N14}); without it, the edge selections cross only inside the countably additive tie sets (Corollary~\ref{cor:N22p}). Neither alternative changes the configuration. In origin II the structure items transfer through Theorem~\ref{thm:N21} in \src{M2}'s setting.
\item[] \emph{Split.} In \cfg{V0}, $\Lambda_1=M$: world~1 has no endorser with a nonzero countably additive part. In \cfg{V+}, world~1 does not refine its countably additive veto $\Phi_1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:N27}(d), refereed once; inputs Theorem~\ref{thm:L34}, Proposition~\ref{prop:M12}, Corollary~\ref{cor:L4V}). With (RL) partners, as in origin II, world~1 is moreover not (Loc) (Theorem~\ref{thm:H12}).
\end{itemize}
\emph{Question for \cfg{V0}: Q$_{\mathrm{N2}}$} (\src{N2} \S6). Is there a full two-world system on $\M_U$, next to an additive world, in which world~1 has no countably additive endorsing part (blind set $M$, $a_\infty=1$)? Theorem~\ref{thm:K33} gives one with every axiom except closed sections; Theorem~\ref{thm:L24} reaches every blind segment $c_a$ with $a<1$. A totally blind two-world world has been announced (\src{P1}, round~22, under review). \emph{Flag:} ``\cfg{V0} implies Q$_{\mathrm{N2}}$ has answer Yes'' is \emph{not} proved: no lemma turns a three-world cover into a full two-world system (Proposition~\ref{prop:Q35} gives only the edge order structure, under (Nest$_e$)), and the partners in \cfg{V} add up but need not be additive. Q$_{\mathrm{N2}}$ is a first test, not a reduction (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.8). The question whose negative answer closes \cfg{V0} is its three-world form \emph{Q$^{(3)}_{\mathrm{N2}}$}: does a full three-world system on $\M_U$, with worlds~2 and~3 adding up, have a world~1 with (NC) and $\Lambda_1=M$? (For origin II replace (NC) by ``$\varphi^*$ has $\Lambda^\natural=M$''.) A positive answer to either form does not realise \cfg{V0}, since $T_1\in\C_L$ is still required.

\emph{Question for \cfg{V+}: Q$_{\mathrm{V+}}$} (the $T_1$-aimed lift of \src{L2}, Question~Q$_{\mathrm{L2}}$). Does a full three-world system on $\M_U$, with worlds~2 and~3 adding up, have a world~1 with (NC) whose blind set contains $M\cap\{g_1>0\}$ and whose visible set is non-null and contained in $\{g_1<0\}\setminus\cl D_{T_1}$? \emph{No} closes \cfg{V+}, because (V1) is a proved consequence of \cfg{V+}. \emph{Yes} is the shape a construction must have, ``\src{L2} on each edge at $e_1$'' (a description, not a theorem; \src{L2} itself is the two-world edge picture), and realises \cfg{V+} only together with $T_1\in\C_L$. With (RL) partners such a world~1 must also fail (Loc), against the spirit of Conjecture~\ref{conj:L2C}; if that conjecture holds, the partners would need endorsers with nonzero purely finitely additive parts (\src{N12\_referee} \S2.8).
\item \cfg{P0}: two or more blind worlds, $p^*$ interior, blind sets pairwise null. \emph{Structure:} $c^*\ne0$ a.e., so every $B_q$ is coherent (Theorem~\ref{thm:L41}(b) with the referee's hypothesis); every $\Lambda_i$ is rigid, $\Lambda_i=(E_i(C^{ij})\cap R_{ij})\cup(E_i(C^{ik})\cap R_{ik})$ with \emph{selected} edge or vertex models (Corollary~\ref{cor:N13}(c), and independently Corollary~\ref{cor:N23p}(b); refereed once); and the field-level necessary conditions of Conjecture~\ref{conj:L1D} hold. \emph{Question:} Conjecture~\ref{conj:L1D} in its rigid form: no field with ($\gamma_0$), pairwise-null rigid blind sets as above and $\rho_k>0$ off $\Lambda_k$ has $D_{T_1}$ as a Bayes model at an interior weight. \emph{True} closes \cfg{P0}; \emph{false} (a field counterexample) does not realise it and is a template. Its proof needs the world-by-world bootstrap of \src{L1\_referee} \S7; with one blind world it is Theorem~\ref{thm:L1}.
\item \cfg{PD}: two or more blind worlds, $p^*$ interior, some overlap. \emph{Structure:} the edge dichotomy of Theorem~\ref{thm:N12} holds on every ordered pair; every exchange of Theorem~\ref{thm:M17} is of type (vis), (int$_i$) or (int$_j$) (Theorem~\ref{thm:N24}); excluded inside \cfg{PD} are the $T_1$-shadow (Corollaries~\ref{cor:N13}(a), \ref{cor:N26}(a)), every one-sided exact shadow (Theorem~\ref{thm:N27}(a)), and exact shadow-blindness at one world next to a partner that sees $J_j\cup J_k$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:M111}); all refereed once. \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$[int, overlap]:} is there a field $c=(\rho_k\sigma_k)$ with ($\gamma_0$), $B_q$ coherent whenever $c\ne0$ a.e., $A(c)\cap\Di\ne\varnothing$, some $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j$ non-null, and on every ordered pair the dichotomy of Theorem~\ref{thm:N12} with ``selected'' replaced by ``a coherent between model $D_K$ with $K\cap[e_i,e_j]\ne\varnothing$ and $K\subseteq\co(K'\cup[e_i,e_j])$'' (as in Lemma~\ref{lem:K37p})? \emph{No} closes \cfg{PD} (via Theorems~\ref{thm:L41} and~\ref{thm:N12}); \emph{Yes} does not realise it. By Corollary~\ref{cor:M11p}(c), no question about the field alone, without the dichotomy, can close it.
\item \cfg{E}: $p^*$ forced onto an edge. \emph{Structure:} $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\supseteq J_l$, which is non-null (Proposition~\ref{prop:L43}), so $b\ge2$. For every $p^*\in A^*$ on the edge, with $\theta_0=p^*_i/(p^*_i+p^*_j)$, $c^{ij}_T$ is $\theta_0$-Bayes and the edge tie set $Z_{\theta_0}\cap R_{ij}$ is non-null, the joint blind set counting as ties (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(a), (c); refereed once). If $I^*\coloneqq\{p_i/(p_i+p_j):p\in A^*\}$ is a non-degenerate interval, the joint blind set $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\cap R_{ij}$ is non-null (proved in \src{R21} from Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(a), unrefereed: the sets $Z_\theta\setminus\{\rho_i=\rho_j=0\}$ are pairwise disjoint, so only countably many are non-null; compare Corollary~\ref{cor:M19p}(b)). If the joint blind set on $R_{ij}$ is null, the ties accumulate along the $R_{ij}$-arcs of some facet on each side, possibly different facets (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(b), Theorem~\ref{thm:N27}(c); \src{N2}'s ``one facet, both sides'' is corrected, \src{M1\_referee} \S5.2). \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$[edge]:} Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$ with $A(c)\subseteq[e_i,e_j]$ meeting the open edge, $\Lambda_i\cap\Lambda_j\supseteq J_l$, and non-null edge ties at every $\theta_0\in\{p_i/(p_i+p_j):p\in A(c)\}$. \emph{No} closes \cfg{E}; \emph{Yes} gives a template only.
\item \cfg{X}: $p^*$ at a vertex, with a second blind world. \emph{Structure:} $\Lambda_i\supseteq E_i(T_1)\cap M$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:M11}(b)); the dichotomy of Theorem~\ref{thm:N12} holds on every ordered pair; on both edges at $e_i$ the exchanges are internal to $\Lambda_i$ or have jointly blind targets (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(c) with $\theta_0=1$); $\Lambda_i=E_i(T_1)\cap M$ is excluded wherever a partner sees $c^{ij}_T$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:N26}); Proposition~\ref{prop:M12} does not apply, since it needs $\rho_j,\rho_k>0$. \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$[vtx]:} Q$_{\mathrm{N1}}$ with $A(c)=\{e_i\}$ and a second non-null blind set. \emph{No} closes \cfg{X}; \emph{Yes} gives a template only.
\end{itemize}

\emph{The configurations on other domains.}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \cfg{GS}: nothing is known. A CONJECTURE of \src{M23\_referee}: the forced device of Theorem~\ref{thm:M24} transfers to the ladder when the partners have positive leading ladder densities. \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{GS}}$:} does any full system on a decomposable domain with (LF) have a world failing (NC) on its ladder? \emph{No} closes \cfg{GS}.
\item \cfg{GL}: some ladder density vanishes on a non-null subset of its ladder (Theorem~\ref{thm:M310}, contrapositive); if $p^*$ lies on an edge or at a vertex, both ladder steps are jointly blind on the joint $T_1$-error sets of the worlds of $\supp p^*$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:M34}(d)); and $\sum_kp^*_k(r^{\mathrm w}_k-r^{\mathrm s}_k)\ge0$ a.e.\ on $T_1$'s silent two-sided pairs at every fixed point (Proposition~\ref{prop:M32}(b), proved in a referee report). \emph{Question Q$_{\mathrm{M3}}$(a):} can the maximal ladder field of a cover on an (Av)-domain be degenerate? \emph{No} closes \cfg{GL}. \emph{Remark} (proved in \src{R21}, a sketch, unrefereed): a two-sided analogue of $c^T$ exists at field level, with ladder densities vanishing on every step at which $T_1$'s advice is not of rank~0, $r^{\mathrm s}\equiv0$ on $T_1$'s silent pairs and $r^{\mathrm w}>0$ there; its Bayes model is $T_1$ at every $q\in\Di$, so ($\gamma_0$) and admissibility hold everywhere. So, as on $\M_U$, \cfg{GL} cannot be closed by the field alone; it needs ladder versions of Theorems~\ref{thm:N21} and~\ref{thm:N12}, which have not been written.
\item \cfg{GnAv-nd}: \emph{Question:} Conjecture~\ref{conj:M3C}, with the referee's completion. \emph{True} closes \cfg{GnAv-nd}.
\item \cfg{GnAv-d}: unaddressed; no question sharper than the configuration itself has been formulated.
\end{itemize}

\emph{How the earlier questions sit in the tree} (\src{R21} \S5). (RL) splits only node II; in node I, (RL) partners add facts to \cfg{V} (world~1 not (Loc)) but split nothing. Countably additive endorsement splits \cfg{V} into \cfg{V0} and \cfg{V+}; in \cfg{P0}--\cfg{X} a null $V_k$ is allowed and splits nothing. Every surviving leaf on $\M_U$ has $b\ge1$. Nestedness of edges never splits a leaf. (M1) worlds with (NC) lie in node I, their certificates' negative sets being blind (Proposition~\ref{prop:L44}(a)); strongly (M1) worlds lie in node II. Sheltering and protection by ends (parts~(f$'$) and (f$''$) of \S\ref{sec:open-core}) are not separate leaves: every such cover lies in some leaf above, and an answer to Question~J1.Q, J1.Q$'$ or J1.Q$'_\infty$ closes only its intersection with those leaves (the identification of sheltering with joint blindness is a reading, Proposition~\ref{prop:L44}).

\emph{Branches not yet addressed beyond the first cut} (\src{R21} \S5): \cfg{S} (only Proposition~\ref{prop:M27}; no full system with a world failing (NC) is known); \cfg{E} (only Theorems~\ref{thm:N25} and~\ref{thm:N27}(b), (c)); \cfg{X} (only the generic edge tools; flagged in \src{M1\_referee} \S6.5); \cfg{PD} (only Theorem~\ref{thm:N12}, the shadow exclusions and Proposition~\ref{prop:M111}); \cfg{P0} (Conjecture~\ref{conj:L1D}; the rigid shapes of Corollaries~\ref{cor:N13}(c) and~\ref{cor:N23p}(b) are the input the induction needs, and it has not been run); on other domains, \cfg{GS}, \cfg{GL} (no ranking-level tool on two-sided domains), \cfg{GnAv-nd} (Conjecture~\ref{conj:M3C} is open, and even rankings that add up are not excluded there) and \cfg{GnAv-d}. \emph{Fixable gaps on closed branches:} I.1(\cfg{int}) is closed only at CHECKED level (case (II)); \cfg{G0} only at CHECKED level, with gap (ii) of Proposition~\ref{prop:M39}; Lemma~\ref{lem:L17} rests on Lemma~\ref{lem:L17z}, proved in a referee report; the one-sided restatement of \src{N2}'s N2.5(b) has been made (Theorem~\ref{thm:N25}(b)). \emph{Reductions that are not proved:} \cfg{V0} implies a positive answer to Q$_{\mathrm{N2}}$; and \src{N2}'s ``\cfg{V+} is \src{L2} on each edge'' is a description, not a theorem.

\subsection{Other targets and more worlds}\label{sec:open-other}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Other triangles.} Theorem~\ref{thm:main} covers every all-facing triangle in general position. For the crossing classes $(1,2,3)$ and non-facing $(2,2,2)$ the analogue is \src{R15} Conjecture R15, supported by numerics on about 1340 random triangles ($\min\Lambda_{\max}=1.0045$ for $(1,2,3)$, $1.2187$ for $(2,2,2)$; corrected values in \src{R18} \S7). The first-order arguments of \S\S4.1--4.5 apply facet by facet wherever a facet has a crossing with a shared positive coordinate; the pinching algebra is specific to the all-facing class, and for $(1,2,3)$ a nondegeneracy at the one-crossing facet is needed (\src{R18} \S5). \emph{Status:} open.
\item \emph{Segments and boundary targets} ($T_3$, $T_4$): open. Several lemmas need $\dim K=2$ (\src{R12} \S1 repair; \src{R1} Lemma 3.5).
\item \emph{$n\ge4$.} Not addressed. Vertex confinement, Lemma UVN, Lemma M, \src{R10b} Thm.~PL and Cor.~PL2 hold in every $n$; Theorem~\ref{thm:ccibu}, the box/corner system and the pinching are three-world arguments. On all-model domains, v3's additive obstruction excludes full additive coverage of targets with three vertices of $\Delta$ (\src{Full Coverage \dots v3}, App.~C).
\end{itemize}

\section{Positive results and approximation}\label{sec:positive}
\begin{sloppypar}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \emph{Gauge mixtures.} For compact convex $M_i\subseteq\R^3_{\ge0}\setminus0$ with $a_ie_i\in M_i$ and $\nu(M_i)\subseteq\co(\nu(M_j)\cup\{e_i\})$ ($\nu$ = normalisation), the penalties built from $f_i(h)=\min_{m\in M_i}m\cdot h$ give an additive system on a decomposable domain whose Bayes model at every $p\in\Delta$ is unique and equals $D_{K_p}$, $K_p=\nu(\sum_ip_iM_i)$; every interior $K_{p^*}$ is covered with (LF) (\src{R10a} Thm.~M; refereed once, \src{R12}). Examples include a regular hexagon around $u$ and 9-gons converging to $T_1$ in the Hausdorff metric (\src{R10a} Prop.~M$'$; refereed once, \src{R12}). No gauge mixture covers a triangle in general position (\src{R10a} Thm.~R, ray lemma; refereed once).
\item \emph{Other covered classes.} Precise models; normalised boxes and their conditional closures (\src{Conditional Shunning of Error.tex}); every coherent target when $n=2$ (\src{Full Coverage \dots v3}); the vacuous model under its accepted exception.
\item \emph{Approximation.} For an interior triangle $L$ and its parallel bodies, $\lp_{L+rB}(g)=\lp_L(g)-r\|P_Hg\|$, so $D_{L+rB}\uparrow D_L$ as $r\downarrow0$; parallel bodies are covered (CPM manuscript v19, cone domains). This is a genuine approximation result, but the representable class is not closed in the target topology: flat facets appear only at $r=0$ (\src{CONTAMINATION\_NOGO\_SCOPE\_AND\_GEOMETRY.md} \S\S4--5).
\item \emph{Earlier no-go for continuous maps.} For continuous, positively homogeneous coherence-preserving maps with weak, generically strict coordinate signs, the three-state contamination triangle at any interior baseline has no realiser at any interior prior, by the same facet maps, corner equations and box as in Proposition~\ref{prop:T1} (\src{CONTAMINATION\_NOGO\_SCOPE\_AND\_GEOMETRY.md} \S2; earlier work, not re-refereed here). In the ranking setting, on domains non-adjacent near the target, Theorem~\ref{thm:main} needs no continuity assumption; on general decomposable domains with (LF) the answer is also negative, again with no continuity assumption (Theorem~\ref{thm:gm}).
\end{itemize}
\end{sloppypar}
